articles.title: „Das hatten wir so überhaupt nicht erwartet": Supererde überrascht Forscher
articles.text:
Supererde überrascht Forscher: Zweieinhalbmal so groß wie die Erde – aber ohne die erwartete Gashülle
Er trägt den Namen GJ 523b und hat einen etwa 2,5-mal größeren Durchmesser als die Erde: Ein neu entdeckter Exoplanet begeistert die Wissenschaft, denn er hat die 23-fache Masse unserer Erde. Welten dieser Größe und Dichte werden als „Supererden“ bezeichnet – ein informeller Begriff für ungewöhnlich massereiche, vorwiegend aus Gestein bestehende Planeten.
Forscher hatten beträchtliche Gashülle erwartet
Laut einer Pressemitteilung der University of Wisconsin–Madison (USA) deutet die hohe Dichte von GJ 523b darauf hin, dass er über eine relativ geringe Atmosphäre verfügt. Das ist bemerkenswert, da Astronom:innen bei einem Planeten dieser Größe normalerweise eine beträchtliche Gashülle erwarten würden.
„Das hatten wir so überhaupt nicht erwartet“, erklärte Max Kroft, der Hauptautor der Studie. „Dichte Planeten dieser Art sind zwar keine Seltenheit, doch handelt es sich dabei meist um kleine Gesteinsplaneten, die der Erde oder dem Merkur ähneln. Dieser Planet ist jedoch zweieinhalbmal so groß wie die Erde.“
Die Supererde ist mit ihren knapp 170 Millionen Jahren noch relativ jung
GJ 523b wurde zunächst vom Nasa-Teleskop TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) identifiziert. Durch die Kombination dieser Daten mit jenen eines Teleskops am Kitt-Peak-Nationalobservatorium in Arizona (USA) errechnete das Wissenschaftsteam die Masse und den Radius der Supererde. Sie umkreist ihren Stern alle 17,75 Tage und ist der Studie zufolge mit einem geschätzten Alter von knapp 170 Millionen Jahren noch relativ jung.
Diese Kombination aus Größe, Masse und geringem Alter stellt die gängigen Modelle zur Planetenentstehung laut space.com vor ein Rätsel. Denn anders als große Planeten unseres Sonnensystems wie Jupiter und Saturn, die schon früh begannen, ihre massiven Gashüllen rasch anzureichern, deutet die ungewöhnlich hohe Dichte von GJ 523b darauf hin, dass sie über relativ wenig Gas verfügt und überwiegend aus Gestein besteht.
Handelt es sich bei dieser ungewöhnlichen Supererde um eine Ausnahme?
Das wirft die Frage auf, warum diese Supererde eine so andere Entwicklung nahm. „Die Frage ist: Warum hat dieser Planet das nicht getan, obwohl er 20-mal so groß ist wie die Erde?“, betonte Kroft in der Pressemitteilung.
Die Entdeckung weiterer Exoplaneten wie GJ 523b könnte Aufschluss darüber geben, ob es sich bei dieser ungewöhnlichen Supererde um eine seltene Ausnahme oder um einen Teil einer größeren Population handelt. „Es ist schwierig, von einer Stichprobengröße von eins auf die Planetenentstehung im Allgemeinen zu schließen“, sagte Kroft. „Wir werden zwar nicht auf 10.000 dieser extrem dichten Planeten kommen, aber wenn wir 20 oder 30 finden, könnten sich vielleicht gewisse Trends abzeichnen.“

articles.title: Domain and publish date filters for Web Search on AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Domain and publish date filters for Web Search on AgentCore
When an AI agent uses Web Search to ground its answers on behalf of a customer, the organization behind that agent needs domain and date filters to control which sources the agent consults and how fresh those sources must be. A financial-services agent shouldn’t ground its answers in an unvetted blog. A product-information agent shouldn’t cite pricing or inventory data from three years ago when the user asked about current availability, as stock levels and pricing change rapidly.
Today, we’re announcing runtime domain and published-date filtering for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale with any framework or model. This capability ships as part of the web-search connector version 1.2.0. These capabilities give developers per-call control over which web domains their agents can search and what publication-date window results must fall within, all enforced server-side. No external orchestration is required. When combined with existing admin-level domain policies, organizations have a layered filtering model that enforces enterprise governance while giving individual API calls the flexibility to narrow scope dynamically, per request.
Alongside runtime filtering, this release also expands Web Search availability to two new AWS Regions: eu-west-1 (Dublin) and ap-northeast-1 (Tokyo). Customers in Europe and Asia Pacific can now invoke Web Search from a regional endpoint closer to their workloads, reducing latency and providing an EU-based entry point for organizations with data proximity requirements. AgentCore uses a zero-egress architecture where search queries remain within AWS. This regional expansion gives regulated customers in these regions a path to grounded agents without routing traffic across the Atlantic.
In this post, we walk through what runtime filtering is, why it matters, how the layered admin-plus-runtime model works, how to get started with the new API parameters, and what regional availability means for your workloads.
What’s new in connector version 1.2.0
This launch introduces two new capabilities within the filters object of the Web Search tool input schema:
1. Runtime domain filtering
Pass an include (allowlist) or exclude (denylist) list of domains on every tools/call invocation. This gives per-request control over which sources the agent may consult.
| Field | Description | 
| filters.domainFilter.include | Results from these domains are returned | 
| filters.domainFilter.exclude | Results from these domains are suppressed | 
Each list supports up to 100 domains, counted independently.
2. Published-date filtering
Restrict results to content published within a specific date range using ISO-8601 UTC bounds:
| Field | Description | 
| filters.publishedDateFilter.from | Earliest publication date (inclusive) | 
| filters.publishedDateFilter.to | Latest publication date (inclusive) | 
Both filters are optional and applied per request. Omitting them preserves the existing behavior where all indexed content is eligible.
Why runtime filtering matters
Real-world agent workloads demand more granular control than organization-wide policies alone can provide:
- Per-task source restriction: A compliance agent analyzing regulatory updates should only search .gov domains and approved publishers, not the open web.
- Temporal scoping: A market-intelligence agent summarizing “this week’s earnings calls” should never surface results from prior quarters, even if they rank highly for the query.
- Dynamic allow/deny at call time: A multi-tenant platform serving different customers may need different domain policies per request, without creating separate targets for each tenant.
- Content freshness guarantees: A customer support agent answering “what changed in the latest release” should only return documentation published in the past 7 days.
Runtime filtering addresses these needs by moving control into the API call itself.
How it works: The request flow
The following diagram shows the lifecycle of a filtered search request: your agent sends a tools/call with query and filters, the Gateway merges your runtime filters with the admin-level policy, executes the filtered query against the web index, enforces compliance on the raw results, and returns only verified results for your agent to ground its response on.
The entire lifecycle is server-side. There’s no client-side filtering loop, no post-processing, and no additional roundtrips.
The layered filtering model: Admin + runtime
A key design principle of this launch is that runtime filters can narrow but never expand the scope set by an administrator. This ensures enterprise policy is always enforced, regardless of what a runtime caller requests. The admin-level domain lists are set up during creation of the connector resource.
Merge logic
The following diagram illustrates how admin-level and runtime filter lists combine: include lists merge by intersection (only domains present in both lists survive) while exclude lists merge by union (a domain blocked at either level stays blocked). Notice how d.com is dropped from the effective allowlist because it appears only in the runtime list, not the admin policy.
Domain include (allowlist): The effective allowlist is the intersection of admin and runtime lists. If the admin allows [a.com, b.com, c.com] and the runtime call includes [b.com, c.com, d.com], only b.com and c.com are searched. The domain d.com is outside the admin domain list and is silently dropped.
Domain exclude (denylist): The effective denylist is the union of admin and runtime lists. If the admin blocks [x.com] and the runtime call excludes [y.com], both are blocked.
Note: A runtime caller can’t search a domain the admin hasn’t allowed and can’t unblock a domain the admin has denied. Runtime filters can only further restrict the search space.
Filter compliance behavior
When filters are active, Web Search prioritizes precision over recall. Results that can’t be verified against your filter criteria are excluded rather than returned unfiltered:
- Domain filter active: Results without a recognizable domain are excluded from consideration.
- Date filter active: Results without a recognized publication date are excluded.
You might receive fewer results when filters are active, but every result you do receive satisfies your specified filter criteria.
Cap enforcement
There are four lists: admin include, admin exclude, runtime include, and runtime exclude. Each supports up to 100 entries independently. For full configuration details and composition rules, see Configure domain filtering in the Developer Guide.
Getting started
Web Search is delivered through AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that provides a managed endpoint, compatible with the Model Context Protocol (MCP), for connecting agents to tools. Follow these steps to enable runtime domain and date filtering for your Web Search target.
Prerequisites
- An Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway with a Web Search target pinned to connector version 1.2.0 or later.
- AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions: your calling agent or application needs bedrock-agentcore:InvokeGateway on the gateway Amazon Resource Name (ARN), and the Gateway’s service role needsbedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch . See Configure the Gateway Service Role for the complete policy.
- The latest AWS SDK (Python, JavaScript, Java, .NET, Go, Ruby, or PHP).
Step 1: Create a Web Search target with version 1.2.0
Use AWS SDK for Python (Boto3) to create (or update) a target pinned to version 1.2.0, with admin-level domain policies. If you already have a Web Search target on version 1.1.0, you can use UpdateGatewayTarget to pin it to version 1.2.0 instead of creating a new target. For additional setup options, including the AgentCore CLI and console, see Set up Web Search Tool.
Step 2: Invoke with runtime filters
Imagine your agent monitors SEC enforcement actions for a legal team. The team only trusts sec.gov as a primary source, and they need actions from the current month, not historical filings. Here’s the tools/call payload your agent sends:
The agent receives only results from sec.gov published in the last five weeks. There’s no third-party legal commentary or outdated filings in the results.
Note: The tool name in your tools/call request is the name discovered through tools/list, which follows the pattern <target-name>___WebSearch. For the target created earlier, that’s web-search-filtered___WebSearch. The runtime include list (sec.gov) intersects with the admin list (approved-wire-1.com, approved-wire-2.com, sec.gov, investor.gov). Because sec.gov appears in both, it is searched. If you passed some-other-site.com, it would be silently dropped because it’s not in the admin allowlist.
Sample code examples
Here are some examples of how you can use the MCP client created from the AgentCore Gateway with the new filters at runtime. Code sample to create MCP client for calling tools
Example 1: Clinical research assistant with regulatory citation requirements
You’re building a research assistant for a pharmaceutical company’s regulatory affairs team. Company policy mandates that every answer cite only FDA, NIH, or ClinicalTrials.gov. A citation from a health blog isn’t only a quality issue. It’s a compliance violation that could surface in an audit. The agent needs to enforce this on every search, regardless of what query the model constructs.
Every result your agent cites is now verifiably from an approved regulatory source. Even if a WebMD article ranks #1 for the query, it never enters the model’s context window.
Example 2: Stock-update agent, only this week’s coverage
Your trading desk runs an agent that generates stock updates throughout the trading day. The problem: when a trader asks “what’s the latest on semiconductor stocks?”, the agent used to surface a highly-ranked analysis from last quarter, and a trader who acts on stale coverage loses money. You need every result to be from the past 7 days, no exceptions.
The agent’s stock updates now draw only on coverage published in the last seven days. That highly-ranked analysis from last quarter? It never reaches the model, so it can never mislead a trader.
Note: Results without a recognized publication date are excluded when the date filter is active. This ensures every returned result is verifiably within your time window.
Example 3: Investor-relations compliance, primary sources, current quarter only
Your investor-relations team uses an agent to prepare earnings analysis drafts. Two hard rules: (1) only primary sources: SEC filings and official investor pages: never crowdsourced financial commentary sites, and (2) only publications from this quarter, because citing last quarter’s numbers in a current-quarter analysis is a material error. You need both constraints enforced simultaneously on every search.
The agent’s draft now cites only official filings and wire reports from Q2 and Q3 2026. Crowdsourced commentary and opinion pieces are blocked even if they match the query perfectly. Anything from prior quarters is excluded regardless of source.
Example 4: SaaS platform with per-tenant source policies
You operate a research-agent SaaS platform serving healthcare, legal, and financial-services customers. Each tenant has contractually agreed source policies. Your healthcare customer’s Business Associate Agreement (BAA) requires citations from PubMed, CDC, and approved medical research databases only. Your legal customer insists on Cornell LII and official court records. Your finance customer mandates SEC, the Federal Reserve, and approved wire services. You can’t spin up a separate gateway target per tenant (you have 200 tenants and counting), so you apply tenant-specific filters at runtime using the Strands Agents SDK.
One gateway target serves 200 tenants, each with their own source policy, enforced dynamically at call time. Your healthcare tenant’s agent will never cite Reddit or WebMD, and your finance tenant’s agent will never cite a blog post, even though they share the same underlying infrastructure.
Important: System-prompt-based filtering (as shown earlier) relies on the agent following instructions. It isn’t hard enforcement. For hard enforcement, configure allowed domains at the target level (admin include list). Runtime filters passed directly in the tools/call payload provide API-level enforcement that cannot be bypassed by the model.
Input schema reference
The filters object introduced in connector version 1.2.0 adds domainFilter (include/exclude lists, up to 100 domains each) and publishedDateFilter (inclusive ISO-8601 UTC bounds) alongside the existing query and maxResults fields. For the complete input schema and field-by-field reference, see Input schema in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide.
Availability and zero data egress
Runtime domain and date filtering is available today in the US East (N. Virginia) (us-east-1), Europe (Ireland) (eu-west-1), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) (ap-northeast-1) Regions for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
Web Search benefits from the zero data egress architecture of AgentCore: search queries are served entirely within AWS infrastructure. Customer queries are not sent to a third-party search engine or routed outside AWS. For organizations in regulated industries, such as financial services, healthcare, and government, this removes an entire category of compliance review.
Backward compatibility
These features are fully backward compatible:
- No breaking changes. Version 1.2.0 is a minor release. The new fields are additive and the filters object is optional. Existing API calls without filters continue to work exactly as before.
- SDK support. Available across AWS SDKs (Python (Boto3), JavaScript/TypeScript, Java, .NET, Go, Ruby, and PHP SDKs), AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI) and AgentCore CLI.
- Console support. The AWS Console for AgentCore Web Search targets now surfaces both include and exclude domain-list inputs in the connector configuration UI.
Conclusion
Runtime domain and published-date filtering give developers building on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway the per-call precision they need to build trustworthy, policy-compliant agents without sacrificing the simplicity of a managed, server-side search tool.
Whether you’re restricting an agent to approved regulatory sources, scoping results to the last 24 hours, or dynamically applying tenant-specific policies, Web Search on AgentCore keeps you in control with zero data egress, IAM-native authentication, and no external dependencies.
These features are available today in US East (N. Virginia) (us-east-1), Europe (Ireland) (eu-west-1), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) (ap-northeast-1) AWS Regions for Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
Get started today:
- Web Search filtering in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing
- Web Search on AgentCore product page

articles.title: KshatraLabs is building a drone that catches other drones
articles.text:
KshatraLabs is building a drone that catches other drones
The Bengaluru-based company develops autonomous aerial interceptors designed to detect, track and bring down hostile unmanned aircraft, including swarms.
Counter-drone defence has settled into two approaches. Soft kill means interfering with the signals a drone depends on, jamming its navigation or its link to an operator. Hard kill means physically stopping it. Soft kill is cheaper and reversible, and it fails against anything flying a pre-programmed route without needing a signal at all.
That failure mode is why interceptors have gained ground. A drone sent to catch another drone is expensive compared to a jammer and cheap compared to a missile, and it works whether or not the target is listening to anyone.
was founded in Bengaluru in October 2025 to build such products. It describes itself as a defence robotics company working on autonomous counter-drone systems, with a stated ambition to develop and field autonomous robots across air, land, sea and space.
Five seconds to launch
The product is called HAWK. The company describes it as an autonomous aerial interceptor that detects, tracks and neutralises hostile unmanned aircraft at speeds upwards of 89.5 metres per second, around 300 km/h, with launch readiness in under five seconds.
Those two figures point at the same problem. A drone approaching a site gives very little warning, so an interceptor that takes a minute to prepare has already lost, and one that cannot outrun its target never reaches it.
The design is described as software-first. External sensors such as radar hand off to electro-optical and infrared sensors carried onboard, which take over for the final approach, and the company says this runs on a proprietary autonomy stack it calls APEX.
It is also working on swarm-capable interceptors, meaning several working together against a mass attack, and on a command and control layer intended to function where satellite navigation is unavailable. Both point at the same assumption: that the threat arrives in numbers and the defender cannot rely on its own signals working.
The company says it has completed hardware-in-the-loop testing at 90 metres per second, a method where real hardware runs against a simulated environment, and that it has taken feedback from the Indian Armed Forces on hard-kill systems.
A pre-seed round, and a long qualification road
In August 2026, Finvolve and India Accelerator announced a pre-seed investment in the company. The amount was not disclosed. The stated use is research and development, engineering hires, intellectual property, certifications, defence events and operations.
The specific goal attached to the money is a readiness level. The company aims to advance its interceptors to technology readiness level 6, which means a prototype demonstrated in a relevant environment rather than a laboratory, and towards field validation.
The market it is entering already contains Bharat Electronics, Zen Technologies and Paras Defence, all far larger and long established with the buyer. Defence procurement rewards incumbency, and a certified product from a known supplier is an easier decision than a faster one from a company nobody has bought from before.
KshatraLabs is only ten months old, employs fewer than ten people, and has no announced customer, order or certification. What it has going for it, however, are specifications, test results and a market moving in its direction.
(This story has been researched and compiled using publicly available information.)

articles.title: Cómo cargar un iPhone para no dañar la batería
articles.text:
Para cargar un iPhone sin dañar la batería, Apple recomienda evitar hacerlo en altas temperaturas, usar el cargador original y cuando sea posible, desconectar el equipo una vez que la carga esté completa.
La compañía indica que un iPhone deja de cargarse automáticamente al llegar al 100% y que puede permanecer conectado durante la noche.
Asimismo, la empresa tecnológica explica que el proceso de carga está directamente relacionado con los hábitos de uso, los cuales impactan directamente al vida útil del dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
Paso a paso para cargar un iPhone y no dañar la batería
El paso a paso para cargar un iPhone y no dañar la batería es el siguiente:
- Cargar el iPhone aunque la batería no esté completamente descargada.
- Desconectarlo cuando ya esté completamente cargado, cuando sea posible.
- Usar Recarga optimizada (activada de forma predeterminada) para reducir el tiempo que pasa al 100% y cargarlo “justo a tiempo”.
- Usarlo, idealmente, entre 16 y 22 °C (62 y 72 °F).
- Evitar usarlo o cargarlo por encima de 35 °C (95 °F).
- Considerar que en ambientes muy fríos puede haber una disminución temporal de duración; se normaliza cuando vuelve a su rango de funcionamiento.
- Tener en cuenta que la batería se calienta al cargarse; cerca de la carga completa reduce gradualmente la corriente para evitar el sobrecalentamiento.
- Si el software limita la carga por encima del 80% cuando se superan las temperaturas recomendadas, dejar que actúe.
Cómo optimizar la batería de un iPhone
Optimizar la batería del iPhone no depende de un único ajuste: se trata de combinar actualizaciones, configuración de pantalla y conectividad, y el control de qué aplicaciones consumen energía. Estas son las medidas que Apple detalla.
PUBLICIDAD
Una de las recomendaciones principales es actualizar el dispositivo con el último software. La compañía indicó que conviene asegurarse de tener la versión más reciente de iOS.
Si se usa iOS 5 o posterior, el control se hace en Configuración > General > Actualización de Software.
Si hay una actualización disponible, se puede conectar el equipo a una fuente de energía y actualizarlo de forma inalámbrica, o conectarlo a un computador y actualizarlo con la última versión de iTunes.
PUBLICIDAD
Apple también sugirió optimizar la configuración con dos ajustes simples: el brillo de la pantalla y la conectividad. Para ahorrar batería, recomendó activar Brillo Automático o reducir el brillo desde el Centro de Control, bajando el regulador.
Para activar Brillo Automático, el recorrido es Configuración > Accesibilidad > Pantalla y tamaño de texto, y luego activar Brillo Automático.
En cuanto a la conexión, Apple señaló que el Wi‑Fi consume menos energía que la red celular cuando se usa el dispositivo para acceder a datos, por lo que conviene mantener activada la opción de Wi‑Fi y conectarse a una red desde Configuración > Wi‑Fi.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra herramienta es el modo Ahorrar Batería. Apple lo describió como una forma sencilla de extender la duración de la batería cuando el iPhone empieza a quedarse sin carga: el sistema avisa al 20% y al 10% y permite activarlo con un toque.
También se puede activar desde Configuración > Batería. Según la empresa, este modo reduce el brillo de la pantalla, optimiza el rendimiento del dispositivo y minimiza las animaciones del sistema.
PUBLICIDAD
Además, apps como Mail dejan de descargar contenido en segundo plano y se desactivan funciones como AirDrop, sincronización con iCloud y Continuidad.
El modo se desactiva automáticamente cuando el iPhone vuelve a tener carga suficiente.
Para tomar decisiones con más precisión, Apple indicó que iOS permite ver información sobre el uso de la batería y el porcentaje que consume cada app (salvo cuando el dispositivo se está cargando).
PUBLICIDAD
Ese detalle se consulta en Configuración > Batería. En esa pantalla pueden aparecer mensajes debajo de las apps, que ayudan a identificar el origen del consumo:
Por último, Apple advirtió que la señal baja o la falta de cobertura celular puede afectar la duración de la batería, porque el dispositivo busca una mejor señal.
PUBLICIDAD
Para esos escenarios, indicó que se puede optimizar la duración activando el Modo de Vuelo desde el Centro de Control, con la aclaración de que en ese modo no se podrán hacer ni recibir llamadas.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: CISA warns of hackers exploiting critical MLflow vulnerability
articles.text:
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that threat actors are now exploiting a critical MLflow vulnerability.
MLflow is an open-source AI engineering platform for large language models (LLMs) and agents backed by the Linux Foundation, with over 30 million monthly downloads, used by thousands of organizations to debug, evaluate, optimize, and monitor AI applications.
Tracked as CVE-2026-64849, this critical DNS-rebinding server-side request forgery (SSRF) bypass in MLflow's outbound webhook delivery was patched in version 3.15.0 and can be used by attackers without privileges to remotely access internal services or cloud metadata configurations on unpatched instances.
"The default MLflow Tracking Server (mlflow server, no authentication, default SQLite backend) exposes the model-registry webhooks API unauthenticated, including a synchronous POST /api/2.0/mlflow/webhooks/{id}/test endpoint that returns the upstream response status and body to the caller," MLflow's security team says in a security advisory issued three weeks ago.
"An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the tracking server makes the server issue HTTP requests to arbitrary internal/loopback/cloud-metadata endpoints and reads the responses via /test: cloud instance-metadata (e.g. AWS IMDS IAM credentials), internal-only admin services behind the network boundary, and internal port/host scanning."
Successful exploitation can allow threat actors to steal cloud credentials, such as AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials, in low-complexity attacks.
Tagged as exploited in attacks
On Wednesday, CISA added the vulnerability to its catalog of flaws exploited in the wild and ordered U.S. Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their MLflow instances within two weeks as mandated by Binding Operational Directive 26-04.
BOD 26-04 was issued in June, and it requires U.S. government agencies to prioritize patching if the vulnerable assets are publicly exposed online, if the security flaw was added to CISA's KEV catalog, if exploitation can be automated for large-scale attacks, and if successful exploitation gives attackers partial or total control of a targeted system.
While CISA has yet to share more information about these ongoing attacks, cybersecurity firm watchTowr revealed on Wednesday that attackers began scanning for MLflow systems within hours after the CVE ID was assigned.
"Attackers are exploiting the vulnerability to reach cloud metadata services directly, and exfiltrating cloud credentials and secrets," watchTowr said. 
"If your organization runs MLflow, prioritize patching any exposed systems, review audit logs for signs of compromise, and check whether sensitive credentials may have been exposed."
On Tuesday, CISA warned that hackers are now also abusing a critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaw in the Windows Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions component.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Apple's services business is finally feeling the pain of losing control over App Store payments
articles.text:
Bottom line: Apple's services business is starting to feel the effects of rules that allow app developers to send iPhone users to payment systems outside the App Store. The changes are beginning to slow App Store spending and weaken the commission model that has helped make services one of Apple's most profitable businesses.
The Cupertino company reported $30.7 billion in services revenue for the June quarter, a record but below analysts' expectations of $31.4 billion. Gross margin for the division was 75.6%, also below forecasts, according to Visible Alpha. Apple shares fell about 9% in the days after the results.
Chief Financial Officer Kevan Parekh said recent App Store changes contributed to the weaker performance, along with foreign exchange effects. Apple also warned in regulatory filings that it "may not earn a commission at all" when users make purchases through alternative payment systems.
The comments are among Apple's clearest acknowledgments that regulatory changes are affecting a business long valued for its high margins. Apple charges commissions of up to 30% on digital purchases and subscriptions made through its in-app payment system. As more developers direct users to outside payment options, some of those transactions can avoid Apple's fees.
A US court order resulting from Epic Games' lawsuit last year required Apple to let developers link users to payment options outside the App Store. Apple cannot charge a commission on those transactions. The ruling changed the way apps can handle transactions on the iPhone and weakened Apple's control over the payment process.
Credit: The Financial Times
Sensor Tower said consumer spending through the US App Store fell 6% in the second quarter. That compares with 9% growth a year earlier. Global spending through the App Store rose 3%, down from 13% growth in the prior-year period.
The research firm said US spending had been "significantly impacted" by the Epic ruling. It also cited weaker consumer spending and broader economic uncertainty.
Appfigures estimated that Apple's US commission revenue has fallen 18% this year. Its data also showed App Store revenue declining in Brazil and Japan, where new app store rules have recently taken effect.
Apple has argued that its control over app distribution and payments helps protect users. Regulators, however, have pushed for more choice. The European Union, South Korea, and Brazil have required Apple to open parts of its mobile platform to alternative app stores or payment systems. Similar proposals are being considered in the UK and Australia.
Credit: The Financial Times
The EU fined Apple €500 million last year over alleged violations of the Digital Markets Act. Apple is appealing the decision. In the US, the Supreme Court has agreed to review parts of the Epic case after a judge found Apple had failed to comply with an earlier order on App Store payment rules.
Investors are closely watching the services business because it has become a major source of Apple's profit growth. UBS analyst David Vogt called slower App Store growth a "concern." Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan said services revenue was "somewhat weaker than we expected."
"It would make sense that it starts to show up in the numbers . . . we were surprised that it really wasn't traceable before," Nicholas Rodelli, director of legal research at Washington Analysis, told the Financial Times. "Apple's premium valuation is predicated on services, and the App Store is really the crown jewel of that," he added. "We think the market is going to reprice the durability of the services business take rate."
Apple declined to comment.

articles.title: China tendrá un radiotelescopio de 110 metros con precisión extrema: podrá apuntar al equivalente de una pelota a 3,3 km
articles.text:
Construir un radiotelescopio de 110 metros ya supone levantar una estructura descomunal. Conseguir además que pueda moverse y apuntar al cielo con una precisión del orden de segundos de arco lleva el problema a otra escala. Eso es precisamente lo que China persigue con el Qitai Radio Telescope (QTT), en Xinjiang: un instrumento completamente orientable cuya precisión prevista puede expresarse con una comparación sorprendentemente cotidiana. A 3,3 kilómetros de distancia, ese margen angular equivale aproximadamente al tamaño aparente de una pelota de ping-pong.
Qué ha pasado. El proyecto acaba de superar un importante hito de construcción. Este 18 de agosto, los equipos completaron el ensamblaje de la tercera capa de la estructura que servirá de soporte a la antena, un paso que sitúa la estructura principal en su fase final de construcción. Según la información difundida por CCTV, el siguiente trabajo será instalar el bastidor de elevación, encargado de sostener la enorme sección móvil en elevación. El calendario actual prevé completar la estructura principal en 2027 y terminar el conjunto para su entrada en servicio en 2028.
Qué significa esa precisión. La comparación de la pelota de ping-pong sirve para poner escala a una medida poco intuitiva. La precisión de apuntado prevista se sitúa en torno a 2,5 segundos de arco, una fracción diminuta de un grado. Vista desde 3,3 kilómetros, una pelota de ping-pong ocupa aproximadamente ese margen angular. Conviene, eso sí, no confundir conceptos: hablamos de la exactitud con la que la antena podrá orientarse hacia un punto concreto del cielo, no de que vaya a “ver” literalmente objetos de ese tamaño a semejante distancia.
El desafío mecánico. Esa exactitud tiene que mantenerse mientras una estructura de miles de toneladas cambia de posición. La sección que se moverá en elevación superará las 3.000 toneladas y el conjunto podrá girar 360 grados alrededor de su eje vertical. El problema es que factores como la gravedad y el viento pueden introducir pequeñas deformaciones en una superficie de estas dimensiones. Para compensarlas, el diseño incorpora mecanismos de ajuste activo capaces de corregir esas desviaciones y conservar la geometría necesaria durante las observaciones.
Por qué tanta precisión. La respuesta está en las frecuencias para las que ha sido diseñado. El QTT podrá llegar hasta los 115 GHz, una región en la que las ondas de radio tienen longitudes de apenas unos milímetros. A medida que disminuye la longitud de onda, el haz de una antena de este tamaño se vuelve más estrecho y cualquier error de orientación o irregularidad del reflector pesa más sobre la observación. Controlar tanto el apuntado como la forma de la superficie no es, por tanto, un refinamiento añadido, sino una condición para aprovechar realmente el instrumento en sus frecuencias más altas.
Dónde encaja QTT. Para poner esos 110 metros en perspectiva podemos mirar a dos gigantes ya operativos: Green Bank, en Estados Unidos, y Effelsberg, en Alemania, cuentan con platos totalmente orientables de 100 metros. QTT llevará esa apertura hasta los 110 metros, aunque eso no lo convierte simplemente en “el mayor radiotelescopio chino”. FAST alcanza los 500 metros, pero responde a otra arquitectura: descansa sobre una depresión natural y deforma activamente una zona de su reflector para formar la parábola utilizada en cada observación. El proyecto de Qitai apuesta, en cambio, por mover una antena completa de gran diámetro y trabajar hasta los 115 GHz.
Para qué servirá. Una vez operativo, el observatorio está llamado a estudiar púlsares, ráfagas rápidas de radio y otros fenómenos del universo, además de integrarse en redes de interferometría de muy larga base, donde varias antenas separadas trabajan de forma coordinada. Sus responsables también prevén utilizarlo como apoyo para misiones chinas de exploración del espacio profundo. Esa combinación explica buena parte de las exigencias del proyecto: no se trata únicamente de construir un plato de 110 metros, sino de convertir semejante estructura en un instrumento capaz de saber con enorme exactitud hacia dónde está mirando.

articles.title: « Canal+ : mauvaise nouvelle pour l'offre de base, un service majeur disparaît
articles.text:
Canal+, mais moins. Début juillet 2026, le groupe annonçait la fin de l’accès à certaines chaînes TF1, faute d’avoir trouvé un accord commercial. Une suppression qui avait déjà eu lieu en 2022 avant que les deux parties trouvent un terrain d’entente.
Cette fois-ci, Canal+ ne supprime pas tout. Le groupe modifie ses offres et laisse celle de base sur le carreau. Toujours affichée à 19,99 euros par mois, elle n’inclut plus le service de streaming Apple TV+.
Vous vouliez un ordinateur portable d’exception ? Les PC équipés de Snapdragon tiennent leurs promesses.
Quels abonnements Canal+ intègrent Apple TV+ sans supplément ?

articles.title: Galaxy Watch 9 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra 2: Full comparison
articles.text:
Table of contents
The Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 are Samsung’s newest smartwatches, and picking between them is easier than the price gap suggests. Both watches run on the same Snapdragon Wear Elite chip and Wear OS 7. They also share the same core health sensors. The main differences come down to size, battery, storage, screen brightness, and outdoor durability.
Samsung announced both watches on July 22, 2026, in London. Pre-orders opened the same day in select markets, and general availability started on August 7, 2026. Both watches are already on sale, so this is a straightforward buying decision, not a wait-and-see situation.
This guide breaks down the specs, compares features side by side, the pricing, and tells you which watch fits your lifestyle.
Galaxy Watch 9 vs Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 at a glance
Here is how the two watches compare on paper, based on Samsung’s official launch specifications.
| Spec | Galaxy Watch 9 | Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 | 
| Positioning | Everyday wellness and general fitness | Outdoor training, rugged use, and diving | 
| Sizes | 40mm and 44mm | 47mm | 
| Case material | Aluminium | Titanium | 
| Weight | 31.5g (40mm), 34g (44mm) | 61.5g | 
| Display size | 1.34in (40mm), 1.47in (44mm) | 1.52in | 
| Peak brightness | Up to 3,000 nits | Up to 5,000 nits (localised peak) | 
| Chipset | Snapdragon Wear Elite | Snapdragon Wear Elite | 
| RAM | 2GB | 2GB | 
| Storage | 32GB | 64GB | 
| Battery | 390mAh (40mm), 445mAh (44mm) | 800mAh | 
| Battery life (AOD on) | Up to 30 hours | Up to 60 hours | 
| Water resistance | 5ATM, IP68 | 10ATM, IP69K | 
| Dive certification | None | EN13319 | 
| GPS | Dual frequency L1+L5 | Dual frequency L1+L5 | 
| Software | Wear OS 7, One UI 9 Watch | Wear OS 7, One UI 9 Watch | 
| Colors | Graphite, Silver, Cream | Titanium Silver, Titanium Gray | 
| US price | $379.99 to $459.99 | $699.99 | 
Samsung lists the Ultra 2’s 5,000-nit rating as localised peak brightness under strong light. It is not a number the whole screen holds at all times.
Feature by feature
1. Design and build
Design is where the size difference between these two watches is most apparent. The Watch 9 40mm weighs 31.5g and measures 8.6mm thick, and the 44mm weighs 34g at the same thickness. The Ultra 2 weighs 61.5g and measures 10.7mm thick. Even the larger Watch 9 weighs a little over half as much as the Ultra 2.
This matters more than it looks on a spec sheet. If you sleep with your watch on, commute with it, or just don’t like feeling extra weight on your wrist all day, the Watch 9 is the easier watch to live with. Samsung built it around a closer fit, using a new lug system and softer bands to reduce the gap between your skin and the sensors.
The Ultra 2 is still a big watch, but Samsung improved it over the first Ultra. The case is 12% thinner despite fitting a much bigger battery, and the bands are lighter and softer than before. Reviewers who tested it noted the improved comfort compared to the original Ultra, and some said the case now sits lower on the wrist and slips under a sleeve more easily.
The Watch 9 uses an aluminium case. The Ultra 2 uses titanium, which explains part of the price gap. Neither watch has the rotating bezel you get on Samsung’s Classic models.
- Choose the Watch 9 if you want a light, all-day watch you barely notice.
- Choose the Ultra 2 if size and weight don’t bother you and you want Samsung’s toughest build.
2. Display
The Watch 9 has a 1.34-inch screen on the 40mm model and a 1.47-inch screen on the 44mm model, both rated up to 3,000 nits. The Ultra 2 steps up to a 1.52-inch screen rated up to 5,000 nits. Both use sapphire crystal on top.
You will notice the Ultra 2’s brighter screen mostly outdoors, in direct sun, when you need to read pace or navigation data at a glance. Treat the 5,000-nit figure as the screen’s ceiling in tough conditions, not its everyday brightness. Reviewers who wore the Ultra 2 in strong summer sun said the screen stayed easy to read without needing to shield it.
For regular indoor use, checking notifications, and everyday workouts, both screens are bright enough that the difference is hard to notice.
3. Performance and chip
Both watches share the same processor, the Snapdragon Wear Elite (SDW6100), and both have 2GB of RAM. This is one of the clearest similarities between the two watches, and it means neither one is faster than the other on paper.
The main split in this category is storage, not speed. The Watch 9 gives you 32GB, while the Ultra 2 doubles that to 64GB. That extra space matters if you plan to store music, maps, or apps directly on your watch for phone-free workouts. If you don’t use offline storage much, this difference won’t affect you.
4. Battery and charging
Battery life is the clearest gap between the two watches. The Watch 9 40mm has a 390mAh battery, and the 44mm has a 445mAh battery. Samsung rates both at up to 30 hours with the always-on display switched on, and up to 40 hours with it off.
The Ultra 2 has an 800mAh battery, which is close to double the Watch 9 44mm’s capacity. Samsung rates it at up to 60 hours with the always-on display on and up to 80 hours with it off. Independent testing backs this up. One reviewer used about 32% of the battery over 24 hours with the always-on display active, suggesting close to three days of typical use. Another reviewer got multiple days per charge while tracking workouts and notifications.
Charging results were less consistent. Samsung says the Ultra 2 takes about 90 minutes to fully charge. One reviewer matched that figure closely, while another reviewer’s unit took closer to three hours. This gap could come down to the charger, temperature, or the watch’s battery state at the time, so keep it in mind rather than expecting one exact number every time.
If multi-day battery life is a top priority, the Ultra 2’s bigger cell is the strongest reason to pay extra.
5. Durability and outdoor features
The Watch 9 offers 5ATM water resistance and IP68 protection. It also passed MIL-STD-810H military-grade testing. This covers everyday exercise, rain, and supported swimming.
The Ultra 2 goes further with 10ATM water resistance, IP69K protection, MIL-STD-810H testing, and EN13319 dive certification. Samsung’s 10ATM rating covers pressure equal to 100m underwater for up to 10 minutes in lab conditions, but the watch is meant for recreational diving down to 40m, not open-depth diving. IP69K adds resistance to high-pressure, high-temperature water jets.
The Ultra 2’s dive features track depth, dive time, and water temperature, and the watch can detect when you enter water. A separate diving app built with Mares, with more advanced dive-computer functions, is expected later in 2026. At launch, treat the Ultra 2 as dive-ready for basic recreational tracking, not as a full standalone dive computer yet.
Outside diving, the Ultra 2 adds Trail Run for elevation and terrain data, plus a Nutrition Alert feature that estimates hydration needs based on sweat loss and body weight. It also connects to external cycling sensors, which the Watch 9 does not support.
- Choose the Watch 9 if your main activities are gym workouts, walking, road running, and casual swimming.
- Choose the Ultra 2 if you regularly dive, hike, trail run, or train in tough outdoor conditions.
6. Health and sensors
Both watches use the same core sensor package. Samsung’s BioActive sensor handles optical and electrical heart signals plus body composition, alongside a temperature sensor, accelerometer, barometer, gyroscope, geomagnetic sensor, and light sensor.
That shared hardware powers the same health software on both watches, including sleep tracking, heart rate variability, a Heart Health Score, Daily Cardio Load, a Fitness Index, and blood oxygen monitoring. Some advanced features like ECG, blood pressure tracking, and sleep apnea detection require the Samsung Health Monitor app and, in some cases, a compatible Samsung Galaxy phone rather than just any Android phone.
Field testing of the Ultra 2 showed strong accuracy for steps and heart rate. In one walking test, it recorded 4,023 steps against a manual count of 4,000. In a cycling test against a Garmin watch, it matched heart rate readings exactly but overestimated elevation gain by a wide margin, a pattern the same reviewer saw across multiple tests. If you rely heavily on elevation data for hiking or trail running, treat the Ultra 2’s climbing numbers with some caution until Samsung improves the accuracy.
For everyday health tracking like heart rate, sleep, blood oxygen, and recovery, the Watch 9 gives you the same sensor platform as the Ultra 2 at a much lower price.
7. Software and smart features
Both watches run Wear OS 7 with One UI 9 Watch, and both include Google Gemini built in. You can lift your wrist and start talking to Gemini directly on either watch. Both also support Samsung Wallet for contactless payments and give you access to the same app store, including apps like Strava and iFIT.
The software is nearly identical on both watches. Buying the Ultra 2 does not unlock extra software. It mainly adds hardware, like the bigger battery, brighter screen, and outdoor durability features.
8. Connectivity and compatibility
Both watches need an Android phone running Android 13 or newer with at least 1.5GB of memory. Neither one works with an iPhone, so if you use an iPhone, this comparison won’t apply to your next watch purchase.
Both watches support dual-frequency GPS (L1+L5), along with GLONASS, BeiDou, Galileo, and QZSS for more accurate location tracking. Both also have Bluetooth 6.0 and dual-band WiFi. The Watch 9 comes in separate Bluetooth-only and LTE versions, while the US version of the Ultra 2 ships with LTE built in.
Price
Samsung prices both watches in the US as follows:
| Model | Size | Connectivity | US Price | 
| Galaxy Watch 9 | 40mm | Bluetooth | $379.99 | 
| Galaxy Watch 9 | 40mm | LTE | $429.99 | 
| Galaxy Watch 9 | 44mm | Bluetooth | $409.99 | 
| Galaxy Watch 9 | 44mm | LTE | $459.99 | 
| Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 | 47mm | LTE | $699.99 | 
These are official US prices in dollars, used here as reference pricing. Your local price will differ based on your country, taxes, and available configurations.
The Ultra 2’s price is sometimes confused with the older Galaxy Watch Ultra, which Samsung still sells for $649.99. The current Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 costs $699.99, a $50 increase over that older model’s starting price.
Compared to the closest matching Watch 9 configuration, the 44mm LTE model at $459.99, the Ultra 2 costs $240 more. Compared to the cheapest Watch 9 at $379.99, the gap widens to $320. That extra money buys you a titanium case, a bigger screen, double the storage, a much bigger battery, tougher water resistance, and dive certification.
Release date
Samsung announced both watches on July 22, 2026, at a Galaxy Unpacked event in London. Pre-orders opened the same day in select markets, and general availability began on August 7, 2026. Both watches are already shipping and available to buy today.
Which one should you buy?
The Watch 9 and Ultra 2 share the same chip and the same software. They also share the same core health sensors. The question to ask yourself is what the Ultra 2’s extra hardware gives you, and if you need it.
For most people, the Galaxy Watch 9 is the better buy. You get the same processing power, the same Wear OS 7 software, the same Gemini access, and the same core health sensors as the Ultra 2, while paying $240 to $320 less and wearing a lighter, smaller watch.
| Buyer | Recommendation | Why | 
| Everyday health and notifications user | Watch 9 | Same chip, software, and sensors for less money | 
| Small wrist or you sleep in your watch | Watch 9 (40mm) | Lighter and thinner, less noticeable overnight | 
| Want a bigger screen without Ultra pricing | Watch 9 (44mm) | Bigger screen and battery, still under $460 | 
| Heavy outdoor trainer, hiker, or trail runner | Ultra 2 | Bigger battery, brighter screen, tougher build | 
| Recreational diver | Ultra 2 | EN13319 certified with dive tracking built in | 
| Wants the longest battery life Samsung offers | Ultra 2 | 800mAh battery, rated up to 60 or 80 hours | 
| Stores lots of music, maps, or apps offline | Ultra 2 | 64GB storage versus 32GB on the Watch 9 | 
Before you pay extra for the Ultra 2, know exactly what you need it for. That could be the battery, durability, diving certification, or extra storage.
A quick way to decide
- If you need a small, light watch, pick the Watch 9.
- If you need diving, trail, or rugged outdoor tools, pick the Ultra 2.
- If none of those apply and multi-day battery matters most to you, pick the Ultra 2.
- If battery life isn’t your priority and you don’t need 64GB storage or the brighter screen, pick the Watch 9.
Alternatives to the Galaxy Watch 9 and Galaxy Watch Ultra 2
If you’re weighing other options outside Samsung, here’s the landscape.
- Google Pixel Watch 5: Launched August 12, 2026, starting at $399 for the 41mm and $429 for the 45mm. It runs Google’s own Gemini-focused software, rates battery life at up to 30 to 40 hours, and works with most Android phones, not just Samsung’s. Pick this if you want a Google-first experience instead of Samsung’s.
- Apple Watch Series 11: Starts at $399, rated for up to 24 hours of battery life, and requires an iPhone. Pick this only if you’re on iOS.
- Apple Watch Ultra 3: The closer match to the Ultra 2 in price and positioning, at $799. It also requires an iPhone.
- Garmin Fenix 8 Pro: Built for serious outdoor athletes, with up to 27 days of battery life in smartwatch mode and satellite connectivity. It starts at $1,199.99, a much higher price than either Samsung watch.
Testing that pitted the Ultra 2 against a Garmin watch on an 11-mile bike ride found Samsung matched Garmin’s heart rate numbers exactly and came close on distance, but Garmin’s elevation data was more accurate. If serious outdoor training is your main use case, factor that in.
Both watches give you the same core Samsung smartwatch experience. Your choice comes down to how much size, battery life, and outdoor toughness you actually need on your wrist.

articles.title: MLflow Vulnerability Exploited for Cloud Credential Theft
articles.text:
Threat actors have been exploiting a recent MLflow vulnerability to steal sensitive information, including credentials and secrets.
An open source AI engineering platform, MLflow allows users to manage the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle and deploy AI agents, LLMs, and ML models in production. It has over 27,000 GitHub stars and more than 60 million monthly downloads.
Tracked as CVE-2026-64849 (CVSS score of 9.3), the exploited security defect is described as an unauthenticated server-side request forgery (SSRF) issue that allows attackers to send HTTP requests to internal endpoints.
The issue exists because the default MLflow Tracking Server (mlflow server) exposes the model-registry webhooks API without authentication, according to MLflow’s advisory.
One of the exposed endpoints would return the upstream response status and body to the caller, and an SSRF protection that was added in version 3.10.0 could be bypassed.
“Attackers are exploiting the vulnerability to reach cloud metadata services directly and exfiltrate cloud credentials and secrets,” attack surface management firm WatchTowr warns.
According to the company, in-the-wild exploitation started within hours of CVE assignment, targeting cloud-hosted instances.
“All MLflow versions before 3.15.0 are affected. If your organization runs MLflow, prioritize patching any exposed systems, review audit logs for signs of compromise, and check whether sensitive credentials may have been exposed,” WatchTowr says.
On Wednesday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added CVE-2026-64849 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, urging federal agencies to patch it within two weeks, in line with BOD 26-04’s recommendations.

Wednesday, August 19th 2026
	
	
	
	
Drakong by Hyperkin Introduces the PixelByte Controller and Blindbox Gamepads
Drakong by Hyperkin, a leading L.A. based gaming hardware company, announced today the PixelByte Controller, a new range of highly collectible, fully-functional controllers, and the world's first line of Blindbox gamepads!!
Tiny in size, huge on fun, the PixelByte Controller range offers a fully-functional gamepad that's small enough to go where you go, and thanks to its integrated keychain, the PixelByte can attach to your belt loop, bag, purse, or practically anything, ideal for travel or for fans who thrive on Blindbox collecting. Impossibly small and equally as adorable, the PixelByte range will be available in multiple series of collectible designs (coming soon), featuring some of the world's best-loved licenses, themes and IP's.From anime, to snacks, games to TV shows, fans will never know what's next with this landmark range of collectible hardware from Drakong.
The first series of PixelByte Controllers launches with the incredible Attack on Titan range, and with pre-orders starting today, you won't have long to wait! A series of seven fully licensed designs, based on the fan-favorite anime, lovers of the show will want to collect them all!
With the PixelByte Controller, size really does matter, and despite its small stature, the PixelByte miraculously manages to deliver a genuine, multi-format gamepad that's fun to collect and perfect for travel.
Featuring three separate modes, each available at a flick of a switch, the PixelByte Controller includes integrated Bluetooth technology, and is compatible with iOS, Android, PC, Nintendo Switch 1|2, Linux based devices and more! Affording maximum compatibility, gamers can easily switch the orientation of the Bumper and Trigger Buttons, as well as the ABXY Action Buttons, as well as switching the D-pad to replicating a left Thumb Stick should they wish. For those finger intensive gaming sessions, the PixelByte even includes an integrated Turbo Mode!
When playtime is over, the PixelByte need not be put away, it transforms into a useful work tool, offering yet more value and functionality! Switch to Productivity Mode and the PixelByte becomes a hybrid mouse/keyboard controller! Used to scroll through presentation slides, take a photo remotely on your phone, access hot keys on your PC, the list of possibilities is as endless as your imagination.
With the finger-sized loop and tactile silicone membrane buttons, company meetings are made just a little bit easier, as the PixelByte transforms into a trusted fidget toy.
Slade Dude Suzuki, Lead Product Developer for Drakong commented, "The PixelByte Controller is a new concept in collectible hardware from Drakong, the first in the world to be sold under a traditional Blindbox format. Designed for collectors, gamers and everyone who values instant gaming on the go, the PixelByte packs a serious punch into an impressively small size. Working with some of the most beloved franchises and IP's in the world, we can't wait to show gamers what's in store for the range, with every design featuring exciting looks, quality hardware, and genuine fun."The Attack on Titan PixelByte Controller range is available for pre-order today and is available from hyperkinstore.com and Amazon for an incredible MSRP of: $24.99 / €24.99 / £19.99

articles.title: OpenAI is slowing down AI development after rogue agents incidents and Bernie Sanders threatens Senate action
articles.text:
What just happened? Just over a week after Senator Bernie Sanders threatened Senate action against companies that failed to do so, OpenAI has announced it is slowing the pace of its AI development. The move follows the revelation that OpenAI was one of several firms whose AI agents went rogue and hacked other organizations.
OpenAI says that two developments over the past several weeks have underscored the growing risks associated with increasingly capable AI systems: the attack on Hugging Face and others by its own agents and the company's decision to slow the release of its new Astra model because it has "critical" cybersecurity capabilities.
As such, OpenAI has added "urgency" to its work on strengthening monitoring, alignment, and containment safeguards across all stages of the training process, requiring it to slow the pace of scaling.
New measures being implemented by the ChatGPT maker include a two-week pause in reinforcement learning training on its latest models intended for deployment.
OpenAI's largest planned frontier RL run also remains on hold while it conducts smaller-scale training and evaluations to assess model behavior, test safeguards, and gather more evidence of alignment.
The company also paused research workloads that allowed frontier models to execute code or access the internet. Some have since resumed under tighter controls, but many involving Astra remain suspended until they meet new requirements covering sandboxing, network isolation, reduced privileges, security logging, and automated attack simulations.
A new multistage monitoring system examines models' activity, tool use, and available reasoning for signs of data theft, unauthorized access, destructive behavior, or attempts to bypass safeguards. It's mandatory for tool-using RL training and evaluations involving Sol-level models or above, and for all Astra inference involving tools.
The company says it aims to generate an alert no more than 30 minutes after suspicious activity is detected. If a possible breach cannot be dismissed as a false positive within 30 minutes, activity must be paused.
OpenAI is also improving reward models to detect unsafe behavior, training systems to be more honest about their actions and limitations, and tackling reward hacking. It plans to revise its Preparedness Framework and involve outside organizations as the safeguards develop.
"Keeping increasingly capable systems aligned is a challenge the whole field will need to address," wrote CEO Sam Altman.
Altman also warned that the safeguards require meaningful compute, with estimates putting the monitoring overhead at roughly 20% of the inference compute used by the models being monitored.
"The capabilities of frontier models are rapidly accelerating. Our ability to understand, align, and secure them must stay ahead," Altman concluded.
OpenAI never said when the slowdown started or when it plans to return to a normal pace of development.
 – Sen. Bernie Sanders (@SenSanders) August 10, 2026
The AI giant says the slowdown is a response to the recent incidents – Anthropic and Meta also saw their AI agents go rogue – but one has to wonder how much Sanders' threat influenced the decision.
The senator's letter to the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta was very forthcoming in its intent. "Let me be very clear: If you do not take appropriate action now, my colleagues and I in the U.S. Senate will," he wrote.

articles.title: It's not just you -- Toronto Tempo star Marina Mabrey frustrated with Rogers Wi-Fi
articles.text:
If you’ve ever been frustrated with Rogers Wi-Fi, then good news: a professional women’s basketball player relates to you.
Someone please help me with Rogers WiFi. It literally doesn’t work 🥲 and they never answer my calls
— Marina Mabrey (@mmabrey1) August 15, 2026
Marina Mabrey, a player for the WNBA’s Toronto Tempo, recently voiced her complaints about the reliability of the Rogers Wi-Fi in her apartment.
Mabrey initially voiced her concerns on social media, posting to X that she needed help with the internet in her apartment and that the communications giant wasn’t answering its calls (remember: the telecom giant gutted its customer service department back in July).
Mabrey told reporters after practice on Monday that a technician came to look at her Wi-Fi following her post, which was thought to have resolved her issues.
Marina Mabrey is not happy with Rogers update 🤣 https://t.co/E8bqA4aAru pic.twitter.com/8URrQNcntM
— Lindsay Dunn (@LindsayDunnTV) August 17, 2026
“He came, told me to move all my stuff out of the closet; that was crazy,” Mabrey told reporters. “I did. he was like, ‘Yeah, it’s fixed… it had to be your apartment number was wrong or something.'”
However, a mere two hours later, Mabrey’s wifi cut out in the final 13.3 seconds of the marquee Indiana Fever vs Atlanta Dream game, because the internet gods have such great comedic timing.
Mabrey noted that her Rogers Wi-Fi is still not fixed.
“I don’t want to be a part of it. I want my WiFi to work. I’m sick to death. I Can’t order anything from Skims, Fashion Nova; I can’t order nothing. I can barely FaceTime. I’m pissed,” Mabrey joked when asked about how she feels about becoming a ‘true Canadian.’ “I’m about to tweet back at Rogers again.”
Welcome to Toronto, Marina.
Honestly, my Rogers experience hasn’t been too bad, but because I am in a pretty rural area, I am on Rogers’ satellite internet instead of fibre optic, so I’m not sure if there is a reliability difference. However, there are tons of complaints like Mabrey’s out there, with customers reporting constant outages and no true fix. Plus, not being able to reach customer service — but that’s kind of expected at this point.

articles.title: MicroSD card torture test writes 133 petabytes of data across 351 cards over three years — cards tested to failure reveal SanDisk as the outlier with 6 failures of the 7 tested
articles.text:
MicroSD card torture test writes 133 petabytes of data across 351 cards over three years — cards tested to failure reveal SanDisk as the outlier with 6 failures of the 7 tested
Which microSD card brands and models are worth your money?
There are many different options available if you want to buy a microSD card, but which one of these lasts the longest? Tech enthusiast Matt Cole wanted to find out, so he set up a torture rig in 2023 to put various cards through their paces and recently released an update on the status of his project on the r/DataHoarder subreddit. Cole said that he has a total of 351 microSD cards in his collection coming from 52 different brands and 111 unique models. Of these, 177 have already been tested until they completely stopped working, have become read-only, or more than half of the sectors on the card have experienced verification failure. Another 107 units are currently being put through their paces, while a further 67 are waiting for a microSD card slot to open up.
Cole has so far tested 200 cards last year, meaning 84 microSD's have failed in the intervening months. While this might sound disastrous for any manufacturer, we should note that the testing conditions are quite extreme, and it’s rare that a user would find themselves in these circumstances. If you want to check out the raw data, Cole’s database is publicly viewable on his website, but he’s also shared some of his observations after three years of testing. First, he divided his microSD cards into three categories: consumer-grade, high-endurance, and industrial-grade. Consumer-grade microSD cards are the typical cards you can get off Amazon, while high-endurance models are often labeled as such (or some other similar wording). Lastly, industrial-grade microSD cards are those that are specifically designed for heavy-duty use and would often come with a data sheet and an endurance claim.
According to the test results, the average consumer-grade microSD withstood 10,000 program/verify/erase cycles, with PNY, Kingston, Delkin Devices, Lexar, and Samsung rounding out Cole’s top five brands.
| Brand | Failed | Total Tested | Average Lifespan (Days) | Average Cycles | Total Written Data (PB) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PNY | 1 | 10 | 643 | 15,700 | 11.5 | 
| Kingston | 3 | 12 | 694 | 23,500 | 11.6 | 
| Delkin Devices | 0 | 3 | 662 | 13,500 | 5.1 | 
| Lexar | 3 | 8 | 684 | 15,800 | 5.8 | 
| Samsung | 3 | 10 | 553 | 11,100 | 7.2 | 
Interestingly, Amazon Basics received an honorable mention, with none of the microSD cards being tested failing yet. They’ve been running for 788 days now, with 16,600 cycles and a total of 4.2PB of data written on them. The only reason they didn’t make the main list is that they’re technically generic or off-brand microSD cards and Amazon could replace the NAND chips used in these cards anytime, thereby making the survey results moot. There’s a separate shorter list for high-endurance and industrial-grade cards, given that the sample size is just smaller and the latter is significantly more expensive than all the other microSD cards available here.
| Brand | Failed | Total Tested | Average Lifespan (Days) | Average Cycles | Total Written Data (PB) | 
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TEAMGROUP (High-Endurance) | 0 | 2 | 404 | 17,300 | 2.2 | 
| Transcend (High-Endurance) | 0 | 3 | 760 | 17,000 | 3.2 | 
| SanDisk (High-Endurance) | 6 | 7 | 452 | 16,200 | 4.7 | 
| Samsung (High-Endurance) | 1 | 3 | 822 | 18,800 | 1.8 | 
| Kingston (Industrial-Grade) | 2 | 3 | 77+ | 141,600 | 3.4 | 
He also listed some of the worst performers per category from popular brands, like ADATA, Gigastone, Micro Center, Silicon Power, and, surprisingly, SanDisk, although Cole avoided no-name brands, since most users don’t expect much from them.
Doing all these tests simultaneously and continuously is no joke, and we see this in Cole’s setup. He runs a single Beelink Mini-S with an Intel N95 CPU, 8GB of RAM, and a 500GB SSD, five TRIGKEY Green G4 mini-PCs and one TRIGKEY K-N100 with an Intel N100 CPU, 16GB of RAM, and a 500GB SSD, and an AOOSTAR mini-PC with an Intel N150 CPU paired to 12GB of RAM and a 500GB SSD. Aside from these mini-PCs, he also has an MSI GE62VR-7RF Apache Pro laptop with an Intel Core i7-7700HQ, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, a Lenovo IdeaPad Y850 laptop with an Intel Core i7-3630QM, 8GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD, and an ASUS ROG Strix Hero II GL504GM laptop with an Intel i7-8750H, 32GB of RAM, and a 500GB SSD.
Running this experiment can get expensive as Cole needs to purchase all the microSD cards himself (unless someone donates them), especially at a time when memory card prices are skyrocketing. Aside from that, he also needs to purchase and maintain all that testing hardware. Although these are either relatively affordable mini-PCs or used gaming laptops, the cost of acquiring and running all these units will eventually stack up.

Jowi Morales is a tech enthusiast with years of experience working in the industry. He’s been writing with several tech publications since 2021, where he’s been interested in tech hardware and consumer electronics.

In manufacturing these tests might be burn-in testing or hipot testing (insulation system verification).Reply
