articles.title: Lo que faltaba: Microsoft rompe Windows Defender, el antivirus nativo de Windows 11
articles.text:
Un nuevo problema impacta a los usuarios de Windows 11, en este caso por la aparición de fallos al escanear sus PC con Windows Defender (también llamado Microsoft Defender). El antivirus nativo del sistema operativo está presentando fallos al realizar tanto revisiones rápidas como completas, impidiendo que estas se completen.
De acuerdo con lo reportado en Reddit, el examen sin conexión de Windows Defender también se encuentra impactado por esta situación. Según se menciona, el análisis se frena cuando se encuentra en un 90 o 95 %, de modo que tampoco se puede buscar amenazas de esa manera.
Lo que resulta de esta situación es que sí se puede escanear archivos o carpetas desde el menú contextual de Windows 11. Si das clic derecho sobre uno de estos y accedes a Examinar con Microsoft Defender, el antivirus de Windows funciona con normalidad.
Por lo pronto, los de Redmond no han brindado detalles sobre cuál es el origen del fallo. La principal especulación en circulación es que el problema radica en una reciente actualización de la inteligencia de seguridad de Windows Defender. Esto, porque el inconveniente se está apreciando cuando se dan ciertas combinaciones entre las versiones de la aplicación y de la base de amenazas en cuestión.
Windows Defender está provocando fallos en Windows 11
Según se menciona, las versiones de Windows Defender afectadas por el fallo son las 1.1.26070.7 y 1.1.26080.2, cuando se combinan con las siguientes versiones de la inteligencia de seguridad: 1.457.222.0, 1.457.225.0, 1.457.226.0, 1.457.227.0 y 1.457.230.0.
Si quieres corroborar qué versiones tienes actualmente en tu ordenador con Windows 11, puedes hacerlo de esta manera. Abre Windows Defender desde el ícono de la bandeja del sistema o buscando "Seguridad de Windows" en el menú Inicio. Luego dirígete a Configuración > Acerca de.
En el listado de versiones que aparecen, verás una bajo el nombre "Versión del motor" que corresponde a qué versión de la app de Windows Defender estás ejecutando. Debajo de esta verás "Versión de antivirus" y "Versión de antispyware", que son iguales y en ambos casos se refieren a la inteligencia de seguridad.
Otra forma de cotejar qué versión de inteligencia de seguridad estás usando es desde la pantalla de Inicio de Windows Defender. El dato aparecerá en pantalla al acceder a Protección antivirus y contra amenazas > Actualizaciones de protección contra virus y amenazas > Actualizaciones de protección.
Si bien todavía no hay un fix oficial que se haya informado, actualizar la inteligencia de seguridad a la versión 1.457.236.0 parece resolver el inconveniente. Esto lo puedes hacer desde la misma ruta que mencionamos en el párrafo anterior. En mi caso, he podido escanear el PC sin problemas usando una de las versiones de Windows Defender impactadas, pero con la versión de inteligencia de seguridad 1.457.244.0.

articles.title: DJI Osmo fans are breaking the shackles of its closed-source camera app
articles.text:
Even if you love DJI’s drones and cameras, you might not love the company’s bloated closed-source apps that phone home to its cloud servers. But they’re the only way to easily review, manage, and wirelessly download your pocket camera’s footage on the go.
DJI Osmo fans are breaking the shackles of its closed-source camera app
Osmosis lets you download DJI Osmo camera footage without DJI’s Mimo app.
Osmosis, a free open-source app built by DJI watcher Konrad Iturbe (with help from Claude) is an attempt to change that. By reverse engineering the protocol DJI’s cameras use to talk to the official Osmo app, he built his own — which not only lets you download files, but also see thumbnails, stream low-res previews, trim clips down to size, set favorites, filter out only photos or videos or favs, and queue up just the downloads you want.
I just got it working on my Osmo Pocket 3 and the Osmo Pocket 4P that I easily bought in the US; it’s also been tested on the Osmo Nano, Osmo Action 5 Pro, Osmo Action 6, and it should work on the Xtra versions of those cameras too.
The app isn’t all that polished yet. While it’s pretty easy to pair a new camera — it automatically detects your camera wirelessly and the app can remember more than one — it always takes longer than I’d like to connect and begin paging through my media.
Osmosis also doesn’t fully stow the gimbal on my Osmo Pocket 3 the way it does on the 4P below, so the lens is left exposed unless I manually fold it away. And when you’re filtering by Faved, you’re filtering the ones that you’ve hearted in Osmosis, not the ones you’ve hearted on the camera itself.
But it might already be good enough for my Today I’m Toying With videos. I’m always left wondering if I “got the shot” on the Osmo Pocket 3’s tiny screen, I never want to fire up the DJI Mimo app to check, and so I always wind up overshooting and transferring lots of footage I don’t need. Now, perhaps I’ll just review it all, delete what I don’t want, trim what I do, and make my selects in Osmosis instead.
Osmosis isn’t the only open-source app coming to replace DJI’s Mimo. I’m looking forward to trying OpenPocketCine, an ambitious field monitor app for the Osmo Pocket lineup that offers custom LUTs (which I as an amateur don’t use) and things like focus peaking and zebras (which I absolutely would because it’s tough to gauge focus and exposure on the Pocket’s tiny screen). It’s from the developer of OpenZCine for Nikon Z cameras, which I also haven’t tried yet.

articles.title: „Speicher voll" – der teuerste Hinweis auf deinem Smartphone
articles.text:
Speicher voll? Fünf smarte Wege, das Beste aus deinen Geräten herauszuholen
Schöne neue Welt: Wir teilen Urlaubsfotos noch vor Ort mit Freunden, laden das neue Lieblingsspiel direkt aus dem Store und drehen spontan ein Video in 4K. Dann erscheint plötzlich eine Meldung, die niemand sehen will: „Speicher voll“. Wer besonders knapp an freiem Speicher ist, kann unter Umständen nicht einmal mehr die Kamera oder Messenger-App öffnen. Also beginnt das große Aufräumen: Apps auslagern, alte Videos durchsehen, Screenshots und doppelte Dateien löschen. Das kostet Zeit und Nerven.
Das Problem kommt nicht von ungefähr. Der Datenverbrauch wächst rasant und mit ihm der Bedarf an Speicherplatz.¹ Smartphone-Kameras machen bessere Fotos, die wiederrum mehr Speicherplatz verbrauchen. Eine Minute 4K-Video kann schnell 400 MB belegen.² Aufwendige Spiele füllen mehrere Gigabyte. Gleichzeitig liegen laut einer Bitkom-Studie rund 167 Millionen alte Handys ungenutzt in deutschen Haushalten – viele davon ersetzt, obwohl sie noch funktionierten.³ Dabei lässt sich das Speicherproblem oft einfacher und günstiger lösen als mit einem Neugerät. Die richtigen Speicherlösungen können die Nutzungsdauer von Laptops, Smartphones und Konsolen verlängern.
1. Der Laptop streikt
Für viele ist der Laptop das wichtigste Arbeitsgerät. Speicherprobleme sind hier besonders ärgerlich: Updates bleiben hängen oder lassen sich gar nicht erst herunterladen, Programme starten quälend langsam. Wer kein gutes Ordnungssystem hat, steht beim Löschen von Daten schnell vor einer Mammutaufgabe. Besser also, wenn man sie gleich umgeht: Der SANDISK® Extreme Fit™ USB-C® Flash Drive ist kaum größer als eine Fingerkuppe, sodass er dauerhaft im USB-C-Anschluss stecken bleiben kann – ganz nach dem Prinzip „Plug & Stay“. Die kompakte Bauform geht nicht zulasten der Kapazität: Der Flash Drive bietet bis zu 1 TB Speicherplatz.⁴ Mit Lesegeschwindigkeiten von bis zu 400 MB/s⁵ lassen sich Dateien schnell übertragen und sind ganz ohne Cloud oder stabile Internetverbindung jederzeit zugänglich.
2. Das iPhone® absichern
Noch intensiver nutzen viele ihr Smartphone. Fotos und Videos konkurrieren mit Apps, Podcasts und Musikdateien um den verfügbaren Speicherplatz. Ist dann auch die Cloud voll, braucht es eine unkomplizierte Lösung für Backups. Schließlich schließen nur wenige ihr Handy regelmäßig an den Laptop an. Der SANDISK Phone Drive für iPhone® schafft Abhilfe. Nutzer können den Stick einfach ans iPhone anschließen und Fotos, Videos oder andere Backups mit bis zu 90 MB/s übertragen. Mit bis zu 256 GB¹ Kapazität bietet der Stick reichlich Platz für wichtige Daten.
3. Die Spielebibliothek wächst und wächst
Auch Videospiele verlangen immer mehr Speicherplatz. Die Spielwelten werden komplexer, die Dateien größer. Das Action-Game Split Fiction benötigt beispielsweise mehr als 70 GB. Da ist der interne Speicher der Handheld-Konsole schnell gefüllt. Wer Spiele nicht ständig auslagern und neu herunterladen möchte, kann sein Gaming-Setup mit der SANDISK GamePlay microSD™ Express-Karte um bis zu 512 GB erweitern. Die Karte erreicht Übertragungsgeschwindigkeiten von bis zu 880 MB/s.⁶ Dadurch verkürzen sich Ladezeiten und Spiele laufen flüssiger.
4. Unterwegs arbeiten, ohne Daten zu riskieren
Auf Reisen entstehen schnell große Datenmengen: Fotos und Videos von Stadtrundgängen, vom Strand oder aus den Bergen. Wer unterwegs noch arbeitet, füllt den Gerätespeicher im Handumdrehen. Gerade wenn nicht immer stabiles Internet verfügbar ist. Dabei sollen Bilder und Videos gesichert und jederzeit verfügbar bleiben – ob im Zug, im Hotel oder am Flughafen. Hier kommt die SANDISK Extreme® Portable SSD ins Spiel. Sie bietet bis zu 4 TB¹ Speicherplatz im kompakten Format. Mit Lesegeschwindigkeiten von bis zu 2.000 MB/s² lassen sich beispielsweise 1.000 hochauflösende Fotos in weniger als einer Minute⁷ übertragen. Die portable SSD ist gegen Wasser, Staub und Stürze aus bis zu drei Metern⁸ geschützt. Der Passwortschutz sowie die Hardwareverschlüsselung sorgen zudem dafür, dass die Daten noch sicherer bleiben – selbst wenn das Laufwerk verloren geht oder gestohlen wird.⁹
5. Überall Content drehen, schneiden und posten
Guter Content ist oft nicht geplant. In inspirierenden Momenten heißt es: Handy zücken und aufnehmen. Damit das Smartphone auch bei längeren hochauflösenden Videos mithält, braucht es eine Lösung, die direkt am Gerät sitzt, große Dateien speichert, wenn der interne Speicher schnell an seine Grenzen kommt, und einen reibungslosen Workflow ermöglicht. Hier kommt die SANDISK Creator Phone SSD ins Spiel. Sie lässt sich magnetisch an MagSafe®-kompatiblen Smartphones befestigen und speichert Aufnahmen direkt auf dem Laufwerk. Auf kompatiblen iPhones lassen sich auch Apple ProRes®-Videoaufnahmen in 4K mit 60 Bildern pro Sekunde speichern. Nach dem Dreh können die Dateien unmittelbar weiterbearbeitet werden. Das Silikongehäuse, der IP65-Schutz und der Fallschutz aus bis zu drei Metern Höhe⁸ machen die SSD zu einer robusten Begleiterin für mobile Drehs. Dank exFAT-Formatierung funktioniert sie mit Windows®, Android®, macOS® und iOS®.
Fazit: Mehr Platz, weniger Frust
Mangelnder Speicherplatz sollte nur selten ein Grund sein, ein funktionierendes Gerät zu ersetzen. Ob am Laptop im Büro, mit dem Smartphone im Urlaub, beim Gaming auf der Couch oder beim Dreh auf der Straße: Mit der passenden Speicherlösung von Sandisk lässt sich mehr aus vorhandener Hardware herausholen. So bleibt der Kopf frei für das, was wirklich zählt: Erinnerungen festhalten, neue Highscores und kreative Meilensteine erreichen.

articles.title: Screenless fitness trackers are the biggest wearable trend of 2026 — here are the 8 coolest you can buy, from Garmin to Oura
articles.text:
The 8 coolest screen-free fitness trackers you can buy in 2026 — from the Garmin Cirqa to the Google Fitbit Air
8 cool fitness wearables to buy in 2026 — from rings to bands
Just as smartwatches — like phones — were starting to get dull, with incremental upgrades every year and people beginning to tire of wearing screens, along comes a plethora of high-profile category disrupters to help people track their fitness without getting notifications on their wrists.
These 'focus' wearables are becoming more popular by the week, and I'm seeing more and more screenless trackers in gyms, on the start lines of local races, and out and about in town. It's no longer unusual to see someone wearing an analog watch on one hand, and a fabric-wrapped fitness band on the other — or a discreet smart ring on the index finger.
Without further ado, check out my picks of the coolest screenless fitness trackers to buy right now, from the trending Garmin Cirqa and Google Fitbit Air to little-known gems like the Amazfit Helio Strap and RingConn Gen 3 — then read on to find out why you should get one.
The best screenless fitness trackers of 2026
Why get a screenless fitness tracker?
Screenless smart bands and smart rings are having a moment. They aren't necessarily new — Whoop and Oura have been around for ages, but both are traditionally premium devices relying on subscriptions. Now, with the release of other smart rings and high-profile competitor bands from the likes of Google and Garmin, people have lots of different options for every budget.
Cheaper devices include the super-popular Google Fitbit Air and the lesser-known Amazfit Helio Strap wristbands. You can watch my video review of the Google Fitbit Air below — it's lovely and discreet, weighing just five grams.
Subscribing to the AI-powered premium tier is totally optional too, while the Amazfit Helio Strap is perfectly serviceable without a subscription at all.
My pick of the bands, however, is the recently launched Garmin Cirqa. The Cirqa is a great device, taking the basic Whoop concept and adding a tactile start-stop button as well as stronger haptic feedback. It also interfaces with the excellent Garmin Connect app to give you useful training information without as much clutter as Fitbit's Google Health app and its AI chatbot tier. No subscriptions here, either, unless you want coaching.

You can watch our video review of the Garmin Cirqa below.
As for smart rings, Oura and Samsung remain the twin jewels of this category, but they're facing competition from upstarts like RingConn and its RingConn Gen 3. Our reviewer said the Gen 3 had "excellent battery life, comprehensive health tracking and a comfortable design, all without a monthly subscription".
However, the Oura Ring 5 is a new launch for this year, and despite its premium price, the Oura platform has become an impressive AI-powered health tool with all sorts of features, from bloodwork insights to user-generated tags like 'bath', 'meditation' or 'meeting' providing context to your fluctuating stress levels. Check out our Oura Ring 5 video review below.

Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
Matt's a keen runner, ex-kickboxer, not averse to the odd yoga flow, and insists everyone should stretch every morning. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Managing Thermal Expansion And Electromigration Through Interposer Design
articles.text:
New deep learning models may provide a pathway for modeling warpage.
Key Takeaways:
As scaling transistors laterally becomes more difficult, manufacturers are turning to vertical transistor designs such as CFETs and vertical packaging to increase device density. At the same time, the enormous bandwidth needed for AI workloads is driving increases in interconnect density between chips.
Yet the fundamental aims of device packaging have not changed — protecting the chip from damage, and connecting micron-scale bond pads on the chip to other chips and to millimeter-scale features on the circuit board.
Currently, hybrid bonding achieves the highest available interconnect density between chips. So-called 3D packages use hybrid bonding to stack chips vertically, achieving the maximum circuit density in the minimum footprint. Through-silicon vias (TSVs) transport signals to the bottom of each chip as needed to connect to either the next chip in the stack or the underlying package substrate.
3D packages require close integration between the component chips, down to alignment between copper protrusions on one and bond pads on the other. They also pose substantial testing and reliability concerns. Heat dissipation is especially difficult because the surface area of the stacked chip increases more slowly than the volume of active devices. Heat can cause TSVs to expand during operation, creating stress and potentially causing cracks and delamination. Because all layers in the stack include active devices, heat flow and signal paths can affect each other in ways that are difficult to predict.
In contrast, 2.5D packages offer a more flexible option. In these packages, chips are placed on an interposer that redistributes signals from the bond pads on each chip to other chips or to the package substrate. The interposer is a passive component, with wiring and possibly capacitors and resistors, but no transistors or other switches. It is both simpler to model and simpler to manufacture than active circuits, avoiding some of the reliability issues of 3D packages.
In theory, the component chips in a 2.5D package are independent of each other. If the pad layout on one of the component chips changes, the interposer design will need to change, but not the designs of the other chips. Conceptually, an interposer functions like a circuit board with very dense wiring.
Complex structures, complex thermal behavior
However, a 2.5D package still must dissipate heat, provide mechanical support, and so on. A change to one chip might change both the heat flow and the thermomechanical behavior of the package. In fact, Hakjun Kim and colleagues at Seoul National University found that thermomechanical failure is the most challenging reliability issue for 2.5D packages.[1] Because materials have different coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE), temperature changes during manufacturing and resistive heating during operation will cause them to expand and contract at different rates.
In a 2.5D package, the chip(s) are typically silicon with copper interconnects, which have a low CTE. The package substrate, molding compound, and underfill are typically organic materials with high CTEs. 2.5D packages span a bewildering variety of options, with interposers that potentially include photonics components, microfluidic cooling, and more. Silicon and polyimide are two of the most common alternatives, both with embedded copper lines.
In a simple package with only one chip, it’s relatively straightforward to model expansion and contraction during manufacturing. Reflow ovens and other processes heat and cool the entire package at once. In operation, though, heat flow depends on signal paths and workflows within the chip. Temperature gradients within the chip combined with CTE differences between layers lead to complex stress patterns.
In a package with more than one chip, both manufacturing stress and operational stress are more difficult to model. For instance, two adjacent chips might create opposing stresses on the underlying interposer and substrate. Rather than a simple concave or convex bow, the stress field could be a saddle or other complex shape. Kim explained that stiffening the package in one area can increase stress in other areas. For example, if the chips and interposer expand more than the substrate, the resulting tensile stress can warp the substrate. Substantial warpage can cause elongated or failed solder bonds. Yet stiffening the substrate to prevent warpage does not remove the stress, but transfers it elsewhere in the package. The bond between the interposer and the substrate might fail, or the redistribution layers might delaminate.
Ming-Sheng Luo and colleagues at South China University of Technology developed a finite element model of a simple 2.5D package with two adjacent chips and three layers of redistribution interconnects. They identified the space between chips and the connection between the interposer and the molding compound as particularly failure-prone regions. For larger packages, they suggested adding dummy chips — bare silicon coupons — to help balance stresses within the package.[2]
Luo also observed that, depending on the system’s environment, moisture absorption by the package materials might be relevant, as well. Different materials will absorb moisture and expand due to differing absorption rates. Moreover, a material’s hygroscopic behavior will not necessarily parallel its thermal behavior.
Managing electromigration
Electromigration, the next major cause of packaging failures, has not historically been a major concern for logic and memory devices. It is an effect of current density, though, so electromigration risks increase as the current density in the package rises. Yi-Quan Lin and colleagues at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (Hsinchu, Taiwan) varied the copper electroplating chemistry to produce lines with either nanocrystalline or nanotwinned grain structure.
Varying the crystal structure to control electromigration has less impact on circuit resistance than dopants of alloying elements, and adds less process complexity than trench liners and similar solutions. In Lin’s study, nanocrystalline copper actually reduced electromigration resistance, apparently because grain boundaries facilitated diffusion. Nanotwinned copper, particularly after annealing, had a strong (111) texture and a large fraction of coherent twin boundaries. This structure suppressed oxide formation and void generation along grain boundaries.[3] Similar studies at ASE Group examined electromigration behavior in situ in de-capsulated RDL structures. Smaller grains achieved lifetimes approximately seven times longer than lines with larger grains.[4]
Modeling for the future
Fig 1: Schematic illustration of 2.5D package with three chiplets and an eight-layer silicon interposer.[5]
The complexity of 2.5D packages, combined with the difference in scale between the individual bond pads and the overall package makes predictive modeling challenging. Finite element analysis of individual regions is straightforward, but the number of regions that must be considered is computationally prohibitive. Researchers are beginning to develop deep learning surrogate models that can reduce the need for finite element analysis. Early results suggest this approach may offer a practical pathway to scalable modeling of warpage and other non-linear behaviors.[5]

articles.title: He probado el Pixel 11 Pro XL y lo tengo claro: es el móvil que va a jubilar a mi iPhone
articles.text:
Probar un nuevo Google Pixel se ha convertido en tradición para mi. Y me encanta. Aunque pueda parecer que la compañía de Mountain View no innova considerablemente generación tras generación, cada año, y cada review que escribo en Hipertextual (ya sea de los modelos insignia o de la gama más económica), me doy cuenta de lo cada vez más maduros que son estos dispositivos y también, muy a mi pesar, de lo que Google sigue haciendo mal o incluso, ha empeorado respecto al modelo del año pasado. Y este año, le toca el turno al Pixel 11 Pro.
A simple vista, puedes pensar que el Pixel 11 Pro (o su versión XL) es más de lo mismo: un Pixel 10 Pro con un nuevo procesador y alguna que otra mejora puntual. Y lo cierto es que (en parte) sí. El nuevo móvil de Google no innova mucho respecto a su antecesor, pero vamos, como todos los móviles de hoy en día. Lo que hace es, simplemente, mejorar en esos pequeños puntos flacos de su anterior generación. Aunque, eso sí, también incluye algunos cambios y nuevas prestaciones para adaptarse a las necesidades actuales de los consumidores y aportar algo diferencial frente a una cada vez más dura competencia.
El Pixel 11 Pro XL también llega para no quedarse atrás frente a los grandes que están por venir. En menos de un mes veremos el iPhone 18 Pro, y en varios meses los Galaxy S27, así como muchos otros móviles de Xiaomi y marcas como Oppo o Nothing. La clave de esta review, por tanto, está en descubrir si realmente el Pixel 11 Pro XL va a ser un digno competidor de todos estos. Y en mi caso (algo que a ti también te puede ayudar), comprobar si realmente merece la pena como sustituto de mi iPhone, que ya está pidiendo una jubilación.
Un diseño continuista cada vez más refinado
Si ves un Pixel, sabes que es un Pixel. Google ha conseguido hacer que sus móviles sean muy, pero que muy característicos, y esto tiene sus ventajas y sus inconvenientes. Como Pros, sabes que el móvil de Google no te va a defraudar en cuanto aspecto y durabilidad. Te puede gustar más o menos, pero hay que reconocer que es un móvil con mucha personalidad.
Google, precisamente, tiene un truco para darle un aspecto un tanto diferente: apostar por nuevos colores. Este año el Pixel 11 Pro está disponible en acabados Arenisca (una especie de rosado con marcos en dorado), Verde oliva, Gris niebla y en un Obsidiana (negro) con unos marcos en mate que se ha convertido en mi favorito.
Además, tiene una calidad de materiales excelente, de lo mejor que he visto en un móvil. Precisamente, en la calidad es donde probablemente Google más ha mejorado generación tras generación. Aún recuerdo esos Pixel 7 y 8 con un aluminio demasiado blando y un cristal trasero que al tocarlo te obligaba a comprarte una funda: eso ya no existe.
De hecho, Google ha mejorado aún más los materiales en este nuevo Pixel 11 Pro XL. La compañía dice que el dispositivo es hasta dos veces más resistente. En parte, gracias a la inclusión de Gorilla Glass Victus 2 tanto en la parte frontal como en la trasera.
En cuanto a la pantalla, un poco más de lo mismo. La compañía continúa ofreciendo dos versiones: un Pixel 11 Pro con una pantalla de 6,3 pulgadas y un Pixel 11 Pro XL que crece hasta las 6,8 pulgadas. En ambos casos con paneles OLED, resoluciónes de 1280 x 2856 y 1344 x 2992 píxeles respectivamente, tasa de refresco de 120 Hz y, como novedad, un brillo de hasta 3.600 nits.
Es una pantalla muy, muy brillante, tiene una nitidez excelente y unos colores muy vibrantes y muy bien conseguidos con el que se disfruta mucho viendo contenido.
Hola, HiLight
La novedad estrella de este Pixel 11 está, curiosamente, en la parte posterior; más concretamente en el flash. Se llama HiLight, y es una luz LED que se ilumina cuando convocas a Gemini. Lo hace, incluso, con los colores característicos del asistente. La idea es que puedas tener acceso a la IA de Google en todo momento a través de la voz y que sepas que Gemini te está escuchando, incluso aunque tengas el móvil boca abajo.
La luz tiene una intensidad más que decente y es visible incluso cuando hay mucha luz. Aunque no se enciende siempre: solo lo hace cuando detecta que el móvil está boca abajo. Puedes activar Gemini con la voz, diciendo el clásico "Ok Google o Hey Google", aunque también funciona simplemente apretando el botón de encendido.
Este HiLight, que solo es exclusivo para los Pixel 11 Pro y Pro XL, es bastante útil para evitar esas distracciones innecesarias al mirar la pantalla cuando quieres consular cualquier cosa rápida. Aunque he de decir que cuesta acostumbrarse. En mi caso, lo he usado de forma puntual para consultas y comandos muy rápidos o directos, como preguntarle por el tiempo que va a hacer, pedirle que encienda las luces, etc. Pero muchas veces ni recuerdo que el HiLight existe.
Eso sí, una función interesante es que puedes activar el HiLight para establecer una luz de notificación para llamadas y mensajes, y puedes cambiar el color dependiendo del contacto. Por ejemplo, si tienes a tu pareja en favoritos y estableces una luz rosa, sabrás que cuando el HiLight se ilumina de ese color, te está escribiendo o llamando tu pareja.
El Pixel 11 Pro lo apuesta todo a la IA
Por otro lado, el nuevo Tensor G6 del Pixel 11 Pro hace un muy buen trabajo en cuanto a potencia y consigue mover muy bien cualquier sección del sistema. No obste, este procesador no destaca en cuanto a rendimiento frente al resto de su competencia, sino que lo hace en inteligencia. El Tensor G6 es el encargado de mover todas las funciones de IA (que no son pocas, y lo hace a la perfección).
Y sí, no solo hay Gemini en este móvil. Google ha incluido algunas novedades muy interesantes, como un modo de transcripción a texto súper preciso que funciona a las mil maravillas. Puedes hablar como si lo hicieses con una persona normal, y la IA transcribe todo al milímetro. Si te equivocas, corriges sin tener que cancelar nada y la IA lo tiene en cuenta para modificar el texto por sí sola.
Otro dato interesante de este Pixel 11 Pro XL, es que ahora cuenta con menos RAM respecto al modelo del año pasado (pasa de 16 a 12 GB). ¿Se nota esa ausencia de RAM? Lo cierto es que no. Como he comentado, todo funciona a las mil maravillas y todas las funciones de IA se ejecutan sin ningún problema.
Por cierto, el Pixel 11 Pro XL tiene algo menos de batería frente al 10 Pro XL: 4.850 mAh frente a los 4.870 mAh del modelo del año pasado. Sigue siendo una batería más que decente, que aguanta todo el día sin ningún problema. No obstante, he de decir que hay móviles con mucha mejor autonomía.
La cámara que nunca decepciona
Llegamos a uno de los apartados más importantes del Pixel 11 Pro XL: sus cámaras. Aquí hay muchas novedades, tanto de hardware, como de software. Google mantiene la misma configuración y resolución, con una cámara principal de 50 megapíxeles, una gran angular de 48 megapíxeles y un teleobjetivo de la misma resolución. Aunque, eso sí, lo hace con nuevos sensores de mayor tamaño que permiten captar más luz.
Esto permite, sobre todo, mejorar la calidad de las fotografías nocturnas, aunque los buenos resultados también se ven en condiciones normales. Y otro año más: la cámara del Pixel hace maravillas. Los resultados son excelentes en todas las situaciones, con un detalle impresionante, una interpretación de los colores muy buena y una exposición que no vemos en otros móviles. El procesado hace un trabajo inigualable y todos estos buenos resultados también se reflejan en el resto de sensores, incluyendo el nuevo teleobjetivo, que ahora es capaz de tomar fotografías con un zoom óptico de 5x y que llega gasta los 120x en formato digital.
Además, Google continúa añadiendo pequeños extras para hacer que la cámara sea mucho más versátil. Este año la compañía ha incluido una opción llamada 'Captura mágica', que es capaz de tomar fotografías de los mejores frames de un vídeo, sin que tengas que hacer nada. Funciona a la perfección, y es la típica función que tú simplemente activas, y dejas que el sistema se encargue del resto. Evidentemente, la calidad es ligeramente inferior a la que obtenemos con tomar solo una fotografía, pero los resultados son muy buenos y conseguimos ese extra de tener tanto fotos, como un vídeo del momento.
Todo ello, se complementa con una calidad de vídeo muy buena, que destaca por su estabilidad, y una cámara frontal que si bien no llega a ser tan nítida como la del iPhone, también logra buenos resultados.
¿Merece la pena el Pixel 11 Pro XL?
Si ignoramos lo que cuesta y tenemos en cuenta que los móviles de gama premium ya sobrepasan los 1.300 euros, el Pixel 11 Pro es, probablemente, el mejor móvil del mercado. Tiene un diseño impecable (no solo por su físico, sino también por sus materiales), una pantalla excelente, un rendimiento que si bien no es de los mejores, es más que suficiente, una cámara que nunca decepciona y esos añadidos que lo hacen tan diferencial.
Por supuesto, no es un móvil perfecto, tiene varios puntos flacos que merece la pena mencionar, incluyendo esa menor cantidad de memoria RAM y una batería que puede resultar algo más floja en comparación con otros modelos del mismo precio. Y si que es verdad que casi nadie va a notar esa ausencia de RAM y la batería no es mala, simplemente no es tan buena como la de otros móviles, pero son puntos flacos que están ahí. Eso sí, en mi humilde opinión, no es un impedimento para optar por este móvil.
En cualquier caso, lo bueno del Pixel 11 Pro XL no solo está en su diseño, pantalla o cámara, esta en su esencia. Ningún otro móvil ofrece una experiencia tan buena, con prestaciones tan útiles y añadidos que no puedes dejar de usar de lo bien que funcionan. Esto es, precisamente, lo que hace del Pixel 11 Pro uno de los mejores móviles que existe actualmente.
Para aquellos que tengan un iPhone y no tengan miedo de adentrarse en el ecosistema Android, es la mejor opción, sin duda. Si tienes un Android y buscas un móvil de gama premium que destaque sobre todo en su apartado fotográfico y experiencia de uso, considera este Pixel. Eso sí, ten en cuenta que este año es algo más caro: la versión XL sale a la venta por 1.399 euros, mientras que el Pixel 11 Pro está disponible por 1.199 euros.
También aconsejo comprobar el precio del modelo del año pasado, pues puede ser una opción igual de buena (y más económica); sobre todo, si tenemos en cuenta que muy probablemente algunas de las prestaciones de IA de este Pixel 11 Pro, también llegará a otros modelos.

articles.title: SA HR startup Jem raises $8.4m Series A funding round to support product expansion - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South African startup Jem HR, a WhatsApp-based HR and employee benefits platform used by over 200 companies and 250,000 frontline workers, has raised a US$8.4 million Series A funding round to support its expansion into a workforce management platform.
Founded in 2019 as SmartWage, and rebranded in 2022, Jem HR started off by allowing companies to provide their employees with instant access to a percentage of their salaries and wages for work they have already done.
It then expanded beyond that, giving enterprises a simple yet effective way to digitise their most time-consuming HR processes, helping them save time and money in order to focus on people. The product gives employees without email the ability to receive company-wide communication, access their payslips, request leave and get access to financial wellness products, all via WhatsApp.
Jem, which raised a US43.3 million pre-Series A round last year, now plans further product expansion after raising a US$8.4 million Series A round, led by Quona Capital, which will support its expansion into a workforce management platform with new products such as time-and-attendance, credit scores and EAP already in place. Products like rostering, LMS, and more, are in beta.
“Jem is the workforce management platform for deskless employees,” said Jem co-founder and CEO Simon Ellis. “Employers have spent years stitching together a dozen disparate systems to run their teams. Jem is now the one place they can do all of it.”
Other investors include the University Technology Fund, E4E, Next176/FutureGrowth, and a group of prominent angel investors, including former Old Mutual CEO Iain Williamson.
“We backed Jem because it sits at a powerful intersection – essential workforce software that lets companies build a deeper relationship with their people, trusted employer distribution, and embedded financial services that save everyday South Africans meaningful amounts,” said Johan Bosini, venture partner at Quona Capital.
“Its WhatsApp-based platform is becoming an important infrastructure through which employers communicate with, manage and support their workforces.”

articles.title: Google Pixel 11 vs Pixel 11 Pro Compared
articles.text:
Table of contents
Google’s Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro share a lot on paper. Both phones have a 6.3-inch display, the new Tensor G6 chip, 256GB of base storage, 12GB of RAM at their cheapest configuration, Android 17, and seven years of software updates. Their dimensions are almost identical too.
The price tells a different story. The Pixel 11 starts at $899, while the Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099. In the UK, they start at £879 and £1,079. That $200 gap raises one clear question: what do you get for the extra money?
Most of that premium goes into a better screen, stronger camera hardware, and a handful of Pro-only features. The processor and most of the software stay the same on both phones. Here is how the Pixel 11 vs Pixel 11 Pro comparison breaks down.
Pixel 11 vs Pixel 11 Pro specs at a glance
| Spec | Pixel 11 | Pixel 11 Pro | 
| Display | 6.3-inch OLED, 1080 x 2424, 60-120Hz | 6.3-inch LTPO OLED, 1280 x 2856, 1-120Hz | 
| Peak brightness | Up to 3,000 nits | Up to 3,600 nits | 
| Processor | Tensor G6 | Tensor G6 | 
| RAM | 12GB | 12GB on 256GB, 16GB on 512GB and 1TB | 
| Storage | 256GB or 512GB | 256GB, 512GB, or 1TB | 
| Main camera | 48MP, 1/1.56-inch sensor | 50MP, 1/1.3-inch sensor | 
| Ultrawide camera | 13MP | 48MP | 
| Telephoto camera | 10.8MP, 5x optical | 48MP, 5x optical | 
| Max zoom | 30x | 120x | 
| Selfie camera | 10.5MP | 42MP | 
| Battery | 4,985mAh | 4,850mAh | 
| Wireless charging | Up to 25W Qi2.2 | Up to 25W Qi2.2 | 
| Weight | 197g | 204g | 
| Starting price | $899 / £879 | $1,099 / £1,079 | 
A few differences stand out from that table:
- The Pro has a sharper, brighter screen that can drop as low as 1Hz to save power.
- The camera hardware is much stronger on the Pro, not just a small step up.
- You only get 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage if you buy the higher storage Pro tiers.
- The standard Pixel 11 actually has a bigger battery than the Pro.
Design and display
Picking the Pro does not mean picking a bigger phone. The Pixel 11 measures 152.8 x 72 x 8.6mm and weighs 197g. The Pro measures 152.7 x 71.9 x 8.4mm and weighs 204g. Both use Gorilla Glass Victus 2 and carry an IP68 rating for dust and water resistance.
Google gives the two phones different finishes. The Pixel 11 pairs a polished glass back with a satin aluminum frame. The Pro uses a matte glass back with a mostly polished aluminum frame, plus an extra scratch-resistant coating on the screen.
The display is where the gap grows. The Pixel 11 runs a 1080 x 2424 OLED panel at 60 to 120Hz. The Pro steps up to a 1280 x 2856 LTPO OLED that can scale from 1Hz to 120Hz, which helps it save battery on static screens. Pixel density goes from 422ppi on the Pixel 11 to 495ppi on the Pro.
Google also rates the Pro brighter: up to 3,600 nits peak versus 3,000 nits on the standard model. These are manufacturer figures for now. Independent brightness and color accuracy tests should give a clearer picture once reviewers get retail units.
For everyday indoor use, the Pixel 11’s 120Hz screen already covers the basics well. The Pro display makes more sense if you want sharper text, a lower minimum refresh rate, or the highest brightness Google offers this year.
Performance and software
Both phones run on the same Tensor G6 chip with a Titan M3 security coprocessor. Google says the new chip brings faster web browsing and quicker app launches than the Tensor G5, along with faster on-device AI processing that uses less power. These are Google’s own figures and still need independent testing to confirm.
RAM is where things get interesting. A 256GB Pixel 11 has 12GB of RAM. So does a 256GB Pixel 11 Pro. The Pro only moves up to 16GB once you choose the 512GB or 1TB tier. The regular Pixel 11 stays at 12GB even at 512GB.
Software support is the same on both phones. Each launches on Android 17 and gets seven years of OS, security, and Pixel Drop updates. Both also carry Google’s current Gemini features.
The Pro adds a few hardware extras. HiLight uses colored LEDs on the back to show notifications when your phone is face down. Connectivity also moves up, from Wi-Fi 6E on the Pixel 11 to Wi-Fi 7 on the Pro, which also includes UWB support.
Cameras
This is where the two phones separate the most.
The Pixel 11 has a 48MP main camera with a 1/1.56-inch sensor and an f/1.70 lens. The Pro uses a larger 1/1.3-inch, 50MP sensor with an f/1.68 lens.
The gap widens on the other lenses. The Pixel 11’s ultrawide camera is 13MP with an f/2.2 lens. The Pro’s ultrawide jumps to 48MP with a brighter f/1.7 lens and autofocus. Both phones offer 5x optical zoom, but the Pixel 11’s telephoto sensor is a small 10.8MP unit, while the Pro uses a much larger 48MP sensor.
The selfie cameras show the same pattern. The Pixel 11 has a 10.5MP front camera, and the Pro moves up to 42MP.
Zoom range tells its own story. The Pixel 11 tops out at 30x digital zoom. The Pro reaches 120x. The Pro also adds Pro Controls, 50MP high-resolution capture, Instant Night Sight, Video Boost, Night Sight Video, and Pro Stable Video. It can record 8K video through Video Boost, while the Pixel 11 caps out at 4K60.
These specs make the Pro the clearly more capable camera phone on paper. How big the difference looks in your own photos will depend on independent camera tests once retail units are out.
Battery and charging
The battery numbers hold a surprise. The Pixel 11 has a 4,985mAh battery, which is bigger than the Pro’s 4,850mAh cell. That is a 135mAh gap in favor of the cheaper phone. Google still rates both phones for more than 30 hours of use.
The Pro’s LTPO screen can drop to 1Hz, which may help it close that gap through lower power draw. The Pixel 11, on the other hand, pushes fewer pixels overall. Which phone actually lasts longer in daily use will only become clear once independent battery tests are published.
Charging is tied on paper. Both phones can reach up to 55% in about 30 minutes with a 30W or higher USB-C charger, and both support Qi2.2 wireless charging at up to 25W.
Price
The Pixel 11 starts at $899 for 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. The 512GB version costs $1,019. The Pixel 11 Pro starts at $1,099 for 256GB, rises to $1,219 for 512GB with 16GB of RAM, and reaches $1,499 for the 1TB model.
| Model | US price | UK price | 
| Pixel 11, 256GB | $899 | £879 | 
| Pixel 11, 512GB | $1,019 | not listed | 
| Pixel 11 Pro, 256GB | $1,099 | £1,079 | 
| Pixel 11 Pro, 512GB | $1,219 | not listed | 
| Pixel 11 Pro, 1TB | $1,499 | not listed | 
At matching storage tiers, the Pro costs $200 more. At 512GB, that $200 also buys you an extra 4GB of RAM. 256GB, it does not, since both phones carry 12GB there.
UK pricing follows the same pattern, with a £200 gap between the two starting prices.
Google has not listed Nigeria, Kenya, or South Africa as official Google Store markets for the Pixel 11 series. Prices in these markets typically come through import retailers rather than direct Google sales, so treat any currency conversion of the US price as a rough guide rather than the actual retail cost. Import duties, shipping, and retailer margins usually push local prices higher than a straight conversion suggests.
Pixel 11 vs Pixel 11 Pro: Which should you buy
For most buyers, the Pixel 11 looks like the smarter place to start. You get the same Tensor G6 chip, the same seven years of updates, a 5x optical zoom camera, and the same fast wireless charging for $200 less.
Buy the Pixel 11 if you want:
- The same Tensor G6 chip and Android 17 software as the Pro
- A 5x optical zoom camera that covers most everyday shots
- 256GB of storage at the lowest price
- Fast Qi2.2 wireless charging without paying extra
Buy the Pixel 11 Pro if you want:
- A sharper, brighter screen that can scale down to 1Hz
- Much stronger main, ultrawide, and telephoto cameras
- A 42MP selfie camera and zoom up to 120x
- Wi-Fi 7, UWB, HiLight, and the option of 16GB RAM or 1TB storage
At 256GB, the choice comes down mostly to how much you care about the camera and screen, since RAM and the processor stay the same. At 512GB, the Pro becomes easier to justify because that same $200 also gets you 16GB of RAM. If you rarely shoot long zoom photos or use advanced video controls, the Pixel 11 gives you most of the experience for less money.
Frequently asked questions
Q) What is the difference between the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro?
A) The main differences lie in the display and cameras. The Pro has a sharper, brighter LTPO screen, much larger ultrawide and telephoto camera sensors, a 42MP selfie camera, and zoom up to 120x. It also adds Wi-Fi 7, UWB, and the option of 16GB RAM or 1TB storage.
Q) Do the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro use the same processor?
A) Yes. Both phones run on Google’s Tensor G6 chip with a Titan M3 security coprocessor.
Q) Is the Pixel 11 Pro camera better than the Pixel 11 camera?
A) The Pro has significantly stronger hardware across its main, ultrawide, telephoto, and selfie cameras, along with extra photo and video modes. How much better your actual photos look will depend on independent camera tests once retail units are available.
Q) Are the Pixel 11 and Pixel 11 Pro the same size?
A) They are close. Both have 6.3-inch screens. The Pixel 11 measures 152.8 x 72 x 8.6mm and weighs 197g, while the Pro measures 152.7 x 71.9 x 8.4mm and weighs 204g.
Q) Is the Pixel 11 Pro worth the extra money?
A) The $200 premium makes the most sense if photography, video, or the sharper LTPO display matter to you, or if you need 16GB of RAM or 1TB of storage. If you mainly care about the Tensor G6 chip, Android 17, and Google’s AI features, the Pixel 11 gives you most of that same core experience for less.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. articles.title: Meet the startup helping Wall Street put a price on AI compute | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The AI buildout shows no signs of slowing. And with hundreds of billions of dollars a year going into data centers and GPUs, compute has become the single biggest cost for anyone building AI products. But for all that spending, there still isn’t a straightforward way to put a price on compute — or for firms to hedge their exposure when the price changes.
Silicon Data just closed a $30 million Series A to change that. The startup aims to become the reference price for GPU rental and an index that a Wall Street futures contract would settle against. The company plans to launch its compute futures trading on the CME October 5th, pending regulatory approval. 
 
On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Rebecca Bellan is joined by Steve Hou, head of research at Silicon Data, to discuss the health of the AI buildout, and why the data is telling a different story than the doom and gloom headlines about depreciating chips and stalled data centers.

articles.title: NASA gives up on trying to rescue the Swift telescope
articles.text:
Plans to rescue NASA’s Swift Observatory satellite from falling into Earth’s atmosphere are seemingly dead in the water. The agency and Katalyst Space announced yesterday that the Link spacecraft will no longer capture or boost the Swift telescope to a higher altitude due to an ongoing “attitude control issue,” but will instead conduct rendezvous and proximity operations to collect data for future space exploration.
NASA gives up on trying to rescue the Swift telescope
Katalyst Space’s LINK spacecraft can’t push Swift back into a higher orbit.
“We knew this was a high-risk, high-reward mission – a first-of-its kind attempt, developed on an unprecedented timeline driven by the Sun’s activity,” said NASA astrophysics director Shawn Domagal-Goldman. “We were all hoping for more science from Swift. But we knew the takeaways from this mission would be worthwhile either way, and we have gained so much through the series of accomplishments up to this point.”
NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory was launched in 2004 to study gamma-ray bursts. While only planned for a two year mission, it later came to be used as a general-purpose multi-wavelength observatory, but a recent increase in solar activity has pushed its orbit lower.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said in the mission update that this “is not the outcome we were working toward, but it does not change why this mission was worth attempting.” Katalyst was awarded a $30 million contract in September last year to carry out plans to boost the Swift telescope back into a higher orbit, which is a lot of money to spend on an ultimately fruitless rescue mission.
Katalyst launched the Link spacecraft on July 3rd, but started experiencing its own issues at the end of July. Without additional intervention, NASA now expects Swift to re-enter and burn up in Earth’s atmosphere later this year.

articles.title: GitHub programmer ports playable Doom to DSLR camera with 3-inch TFT LCD display — Canon EOS 550D with open-source Magic Lantern firmware uses camera's button as controls, even plays sound
articles.text:
GitHub programmer ports playable Doom to DSLR camera with 3-inch TFT LCD display — Canon EOS 550D with open-source Magic Lantern firmware uses camera's button as controls, even plays sound
Can you finish the game before the camera runs out of power?
Running Doom on the weirdest hardware and software has become a challenge in the developer community. The latest feat that we see today has been achieved by lauris-nl, after they built a port for the Canon EOS 550D digital SLR camera. The intrepid programmer achieved this by using the open-source Magic Lantern firmware that was supposed to unlock extra features for the camera. We’ve seen weird and quirky projects running on “exotic” hardware like an electric cooking pot, an Apple Lightning-to-HDMI dongle, or even an orbiting satellite, but this is the first time that I've seen one running on a camera.
The Canon EOS 550D, also known as the Rebel T2i, is an entry-level digital SLR that Canon launched in 2010. It had an 18-megapixel APS-C sensor paired with a DIGIC 4 image processor and features a 3-inch TFT LCD display and a rear mono speaker. This is apparently powerful enough to run Doom, with lauris-nl showing off the game running smoothly on the camera. The up, down, left, and right buttons serve as the camera control and navigation, while the set button is the select and fire button. You can press the Menu button to open the in-game menu, and then the DISP. button to go back while in the Doom menu. Since the 550D comes with a speaker, you can hear in-game sounds as you go through its different levels.
Unfortunately, its developer said that this port only works on the Canon EOS 550D with firmware version 1.0.9. They specifically said, “Do not install this binary on another camera model or firmware version.” Although they did not say why, you don’t want to run into the risk of bricking your camera if you attempt to do so (unless you know what you’re doing). Now, if you have this specific gear and want to give it a try yourself, it’s relatively easy to do. You just need a compatible Magic Lantern 550D.109 build on an SD card, copy the released module to ML/MODULES/doom.mo and create the ML/DOOM/ folder, then paste your Doom-compatible files into it.
From there, plug the SD card into your Canon camera, turn it on and select Doom > WAD in the Magic Lantern Games menu, and then restart the camera. From there, you’re off to blasting demons and the undead into kingdom come straight from your camera. This is a great way of relaxing after an entire day of shooting your subjects, although it’s ideal that you keep your Doom game on an SD card that’s separate from where you keep your photos. If you don’t have a Canon EOS 550D, another developer created a Doom port for the Canon PowerShot SD1000 / IXUS 70 point-and-shoot camera from 2007, so you might want to give it a try if you have it stored in your drawer.

articles.title: Missão falhou: NASA desiste de resgatar observatório Swift e aguarda queda em 2026
articles.text:
A NASA cancelou a missão que tentaria resgatar o Observatório Neil Gehrels Swift, anunciou a agência nesta quarta-feira (19). O satélite, que estuda explosões de raios gama desde 2004, deve reentrar na atmosfera terrestre e se desintegrar ainda em 2026.
O plano original era usar a espaçonave LINK, da empresa Katalyst Space, para acoplar ao Swift e rebocá-lo para uma órbita mais alta, adicionando cerca de uma década à sua vida útil. Mas problemas persistentes no sistema de controle de orientação da LINK inviabilizaram a operação, segundo o Engadget.
O que deu errado
Os problemas com a LINK começaram no final de julho. A espaçonave passou a ter dificuldades para controlar sua orientação em órbita, girando sem controle e causando comunicações intermitentes com as equipes em terra. O sistema de propulsão também sofreu perda parcial de funcionalidade.
A NASA e a Katalyst ainda eram otimistas no mês passado sobre a possibilidade de concluir a missão, mas o cenário mudou desde então.
A Katalyst teve menos de um ano para projetar a espaçonave para a missão Swift Boost, lançada no início de julho. “Foi uma missão de alto risco e alta recompensa desde o início”, disse Shawn Domagal-Goldman, diretor da Divisão de Astrofísica da NASA em Washington.
O que ainda será feito
Embora a LINK não vá mais rebocar o Swift, ainda tentará um encontro com o observatório. A NASA e a Katalyst planejam coletar o máximo de dados possível durante as operações de aproximação para subsidiar futuras missões de manutenção de satélites.
“Esta não é a conclusão pela qual trabalhamos, mas não muda o motivo pelo qual essa missão valia a pena tentar”, disse o administrador da NASA, Jared Isaacman, em comunicado. “A equipe agiu com velocidade extraordinária para dar ao Swift uma chance de continuar fazendo ciência enquanto avançava capacidades que os Estados Unidos precisarão para manutenção de satélites no futuro.”
O legado do Swift
Lançado em 2004 para estudar explosões de raios gama, o Swift foi gradualmente adaptado para outros usos ao longo das décadas. A agência passou a depender dele para obter informações críticas rapidamente quando eventos cósmicos súbitos ocorrem.
A órbita do telescópio está em decaimento acelerado devido ao aumento da atividade solar nos últimos anos. Sem a intervenção da LINK, o Swift deve reentrar na atmosfera ainda em 2026.
A NASA afirmou que priorizará encontrar novas opções para reagir rapidamente a eventos cósmicos e usará missões em operação para preencher a lacuna deixada pelo Swift.
Layse Ventura é editora de SEO no Olhar Digital e mestre pela UFSC.

articles.title: Former Nvidia lab leader Sanja Fidler launches Veeda AI to tackle world models | BetaKit
articles.text:
Sanja Fidler, the former head of Nvidia’s Toronto AI lab, has launched a new startup to tackle how robots interact with the physical world through AI.
The news: Fidler announced today that she’s launching physical AI startup Veeda AI alongside longtime Nvidia colleagues Zan Gojcic, who will serve as CTO, and Huan Ling, who will be chief scientist. The startup will focus on world models, which are AI models that create an internal simulation of the real world based on things like physical, spatial, and movement data.
Veeda AI, which was officially incorporated in June under the name Veeda Innovation, is backed by Toronto’s Radical Ventures and Silicon Valley firm Khosla Ventures. The company confirmed that it has raised $90 million USD ($124 million CAD) from investors so far, as first reported by The Logic.
From the source: “At Veeda, our sole mission is to build simulated reality for Physical AI. Our conviction is that this will become the critical infrastructure layer for all areas of robotics,” Fidler wrote in a LinkedIn post.
The context: Fidler was Nvidia’s first hire at its Canadian research lab, now the Spatial Intelligence Lab, and helmed it for eight years. The lab focused on research projects into world modelling simulations of physical systems, as well as algorithms for understanding three-dimensional data.
The University of Toronto associate professor announced her departure from the AI chip giant earlier this month, writing online that world models are “where the next breakthrough lies.”
Final thought: While the world’s leading AI developers have so far built their reputations on text-based large language models, Veeda joins a crop of neolabs building world models that deal with three-dimensional physical data. Former Meta chief scientist Yann LeCun left the big tech company to start Advanced Machine Intelligence Labs last year; startup General Intuition hit a $2.3-billion USD valuation for its world models based on video gaming data.
Feature image courtesy Sanja Fidler via LinkedIn.

articles.title: Windkraft-Branche warnt: Diese EEG-Reform könnte Hunderttausende Jobs gefährden
articles.text:
Windkraft-Branche warnt: EEG-Reform könnte Hunderttausende Jobs gefährden
Vor der heutigen Konferenz der norddeutschen Regierungschefs in Rostock kommt aus der Windkraftbranche Kritik an geplanten Änderungen des Erneuerbaren-Energien-Gesetzes (EEG) und am Netzanschlusspaket. „Wir fordern die teilnehmenden Regierungschefs auf, gemeinsam auf die Bundesregierung einzuwirken und die geplanten Regelungen so nachzubessern, dass der Ausbau der erneuerbaren Energien nicht ausgebremst wird“, sagte Robert Vogt, Vorstand des WindEnergy Network (WEN).
Die Wirtschaft der erneuerbaren Energien ist dem Verein zufolge für Bremen, Hamburg, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Niedersachsen und Schleswig-Holstein von herausragender Bedeutung. Da jeder zweite Job der bundesweit 436.000 Beschäftigten in der Branche unmittelbar an die Höhe der Investitionen gekoppelt sei, hätten die aktuellen Novellen das Potenzial, den Windenergieausbau bundesweit auszubremsen.
Der Verein sieht unter anderem kritisch, dass Entschädigungszahlungen für Betreiber von Windkraftanlagen in bestimmten Gebieten entfallen sollen, die sie bislang erhalten, wenn ihre Anlagen abgeregelt werden. Diese Eingriffe werden Redispatch genannt und sollen Netzengpässe verhindern, wenn der Strom nicht mehr aufgenommen werden kann. Die Entschädigungen kosten jedes Jahr Milliarden.
Windenergie-Branche: Netzausbau, statt Wegfall von Entschädigungen
WEN fordert zumindest einen weniger strengen Richtwert, um weniger Anlagen von diesen Entschädigungszahlungen auszuschließen, sieht den Wegfall solcher Entschädigungen aber grundsätzlich kritisch und warnt vor Investitionsunsicherheiten. Ein stärkerer Netzausbau und die Ermöglichung direkter Abnahme des Stroms sollten aus Branchensicht zu einer besseren Energienutzung führen.
Zudem drängt das WEN auf einen zügigen Ausbau der Verteilnetze. Die norddeutschen Länder sollten sich bis spätestens Ende des Jahres für ein Verteilnetzpaket aussprechen, wie es der Koalitionsausschuss im Juli beschlossen habe. „Die Modernisierung und Digitalisierung der Verteilnetze muss Hand in Hand mit einem beschleunigten Verteilnetzausbau gehen, um den Wirtschaftsstandort Deutschland nicht zu gefährden“, teilte der Verein aus Mecklenburg-Vorpommern mit, zu dem nach eigenen Angaben mehr als 90 Mitgliedsunternehmen gehören.
Die Regierungschefs der fünf norddeutschen Bundesländer Bremen, Hamburg, Niedersachsen, Schleswig-Holstein und Mecklenburg-Vorpommern kommen am Donnerstag unter dem Vorsitz von Mecklenburg-Vorpommerns Ministerpräsidentin Manuel Schwesig (SPD) zusammen. Bei der turnusmäßigen Jahreskonferenz stehen die Themen Wirtschaft, Häfen und Energie auf der Tagesordnung.

articles.title: iPad : Apple pourrait lui offrir un bouton inédit… tout droit venu de l’iPhone
articles.text:
Après avoir fait son apparition sur l’iPhone 16, le bouton de contrôle de l’appareil photo pourrait ne pas rester cantonné aux smartphones d’Apple. Un brevet récemment accordé à la firme décrit en effet un système de commande dont les caractéristiques correspondent de très près à celui déjà présent sur l’iPhone.
Le géant de Cupertino pourrait préparer une nouvelle évolution pour ses tablettes. Un brevet consacré à un « système d’entrée pour appareil électronique portable » décrit un dispositif de commande intégré à un appareil qui ressemble, dans la majorité des illustrations, à un iPad. Le document ne cite jamais explicitement le nom de la tablette. Apple parle simplement de « tablettes » et décrit avec précision le fonctionnement de cette commande, dont les capacités rappellent directement celles du Camera Control inauguré avec l’iPhone 16 en 2024.
Un mécanisme qui reprend le Camera Control dans ses moindres détails
Le bouton décrit dans le brevet présente un fonctionnement très proche du Camera Control de l'iPhone 16. Il intègre deux capteurs de pression qui comparent leurs mesures afin de déterminer à quel endroit précis du bouton l'utilisateur a appuyé. Ce système permet de distinguer une pression légère, un potentiel balayage ou une pression plus franche.
Apple précise les seuils de force nécessaires aux différentes interactions. La première action se déclenche entre 0,8 et 1,2 newton, tandis que la seconde, plus appuyée, nécessite entre 3,0 et 4,0 newtons. Une pression suffisamment forte provoque ensuite l'affaissement d'un interrupteur à dôme, tandis que la commande peut générer un retour haptique. Le brevet décrit également un « élément de détection de déformation », capable de mesurer la force exercée sur la commande et de contribuer à la détection des différentes interactions.
Une piste étudiée par Apple depuis décembre 2025
Le Camera Control a relativement divisé les utilisateurs depuis son introduction sur la gamme iPhone 16. Des rumeurs ont même déjà évoqué sa possible suppression par Apple. Son arrivée sur l'iPad reste donc pour l'instant du domaine de la supposition uniquement.
La marque à la pomme dépose plusieurs centaines de brevets chaque année. Vous le savez, l'obtention d'un brevet ne garantit donc en rien la commercialisation d'un produit. Mais ce document se distingue par la précision de ses spécifications et par un autre élément : Apple avait déjà déposé une première version de cette proposition en décembre 2025, preuve que la firme s'est intéressée à cette idée à plusieurs reprises.

articles.title: Un an de Gemini et de stockage gratuit : l’offre de Google à ne pas manquer pour la rentrée
articles.text:
L’an dernier, Google offrait déjà douze mois de son abonnement le plus complet aux étudiants, Google AI Pro, avec 2 To de stockage à la clé. Google a annoncé le retour de l’offre le 19 août 2026 pour la rentrée, mais les étudiants français héritent cette fois d’un lot un peu plus modeste.
Google offre gratuitement son forfait le moins cher (Google AI Plus), celui-là même qu’il a fait tomber de 7,99 à 4,99 euros en juin 2026, dans une guerre des prix où il rogne régulièrement le tarif de ses modèles Gemini.
Que contient l’abonnement Google AI Plus offert aux étudiants ?
Hors des États-Unis, Google distribue un an de Google AI Plus, son forfait d’entrée de gamme facturé d’habitude 4,99 euros par mois. Ce dernier permet de faire sauter les limites d’usage de Gemini (et propose 400 Go de stockage partagé entre Gmail, Drive et Photos, ainsi que la génération de vidéos). L’abonné passe outre les quotas serrés du gratuit pour les requêtes complexes en plus d’autres avantages :
- davantage d’accès à Gemini 3.1 Pro et à Deep Research ;
- un accès à Gemini Omni Flash pour générer des vidéos ;
- l’intégration de Gemini dans Gmail et d’autres applications Google ;
- un accès à Google Flow avec 200 crédits mensuels ;
Google insiste surtout sur ses study notebooks, des carnets qui digèrent un programme de cours ou des notes importées pour les recracher en fiches de révision, en quiz et en petites leçons ciblées.
L’offre s’adresse aux étudiants éligibles, y compris à ceux dont l’abonnement gratuit à Google AI Pro obtenu en 2025 a déjà expiré. Elle peut être activée jusqu’au 31 décembre 2026. Pour en profiter, il suffit de se rendre sur le portail étudiant de Gemini, puis de faire vérifier son statut à l’aide de son adresse universitaire.
Les étudiants américains sont beaucoup mieux servis
La comparaison pique un peu quand on regarde de l’autre côté de l’Atlantique. Aux États-Unis, les étudiants récupèrent Google AI Pro et ses 5 To de stockage, l’abonnement facturé 21,99 euros par mois en France. Le reste du monde est un peu moins bien loti avec AI Plus et ses 400 Go. Sur douze mois, le cadeau permet d’économiser autour de 60 euros de valeur (contre 264 euros que représentait l’AI Pro offert aux étudiants l’an passé).
En offrant Gemini pendant toute une année universitaire, Google espère surtout installer de nouvelles habitudes chez une cible qui utilise intensivement l’IA. Après douze mois passés à organiser sa vie étudiante autour de cet écosystème — et éventuellement à remplir une partie des 400 Go — revenir à la formule gratuite ou migrer vers un concurrent devient forcément moins facile. Le cadeau sert autant à séduire les étudiants qu’à fabriquer les futurs abonnés de Gemini dans un contexte difficile pour l’IA de Google face à ses concurrents (ChatGPT et Claude).
